papers.title: Neonatal EEG Seizure Prediction with Quantum Inspired Continuous-Variable (Bosonic) Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: We study short-horizon neonatal seizure prediction on Helsinki-style (HUH) preprocessed EEG feature tables using quantum-inspired reservoir computing. Under strict subject-wise cross-validation on imbalanced preictal--interictal windows, we test whether reservoir constructions shaped after (i) gate-based qubit dynamics and (ii) continuous-variable (bosonic/photonic) dynamics provide a practical sequence encoder relative to strong classical baselines. Both reservoirs are executed here purely in classical simulation on a single GPU; accordingly, we do not claim quantum advantage, but rather evaluate whether quantum-shaped dynamics act as useful, low-footprint random feature maps with a trained linear readout. We compare against Random Forests and RBF--SVMs, and report AUROC, AUPRC, per-subject AUPRC, expected calibration error, and stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. Across our experiments, the CV/bosonic reservoir is consistently competitive and can improve AUPRC over the baselines, while the gate-style reservoir is more sensitive to hyperparameters. These results suggest that quantum-inspired, photonics-motivated reservoirs can be practical sequence encoders for neonatal EEG feature tables under conservative subject-wise evaluation.
authors: Krishna Bhatia, Chun-Yu Lin

papers.title: On the lower bound of the refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture: proof of the cases S_{6,3} and S_{7,3} for 3x3 matrices
papers.abstract: For Hermitian matrices $\alpha,\beta$ let $\A_{n,m}(e^\alpha,e^\beta)$ be the average of the traces of all words with $n$ letters $e^\alpha$ and $m$ letters $e^\beta$. The refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture contains the lower bound $\A_{n,m}(e^\alpha,e^\beta)\ge\Tr e^{n\alpha+m\beta}$ (Tr denotes the trace), which for $n=m=1$ is the Golden--Thompson inequality. We prove this lower bound for all $n+m\le7$ when the matrices have size at most three, and for $\min(n,m)\le2$ in every dimension. In all these cases we prove the stronger inequality $\A_{n,m}(A,B)\ge\Tr(A^{n/m}B)^m$ for positive semidefinite $A,B$, or its mirror image with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged; the lower bound of the refined conjecture follows from the Araki--Lieb--Thirring inequality. The cases with three letters $B$ in dimension three, $(n,m)=(3,3)$ and $(4,3)$, are reduced by an exact identity and the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means to a polynomial inequality in two variables, which is certified in exact rational arithmetic by Bernstein expansion on three boxes. The certificate is a short program in the ancillary files.
authors: Daniel H\"agele

papers.title: The Standard Model with Non-Anticommuting $\gamma_5$ in the BMHV Scheme
papers.abstract: The Breitenlohner-Maison/'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme provides a treatment of $\gamma_5$ in dimensional regularisation (DReg) that is guaranteed to be self-consistent at all orders, but it breaks gauge and BRST invariance at the regularised level, which must be restored by suitable counterterms. We present the complete 1-loop renormalisation of the full Standard Model in the BMHV scheme in general $R_\xi$-gauge, including all singular and all finite symmetry-restoring counterterms. We further analyse the impact of evanescent gauge interactions, which allow the photon and gluon currents to be treated either 4- or $D$-dimensionally. We show that QCD always contributes to the symmetry breaking, so that the Standard Model must be treated as a whole, and we recommend a purely 4-dimensional treatment of electroweak gauge interactions. Our results provide a necessary step towards multi-loop electroweak precision calculations with a fully consistent treatment of $\gamma_5$.
authors: Paul K\"uhler, Dominik St\"ockinger, Matthias Wei{\ss}wange

papers.title: R\'enyi-2 entanglement of purification of the symmetric Werner state
papers.abstract: This paper determines exactly the R\'enyi-2 entanglement of purification of the normalized symmetric Werner state in every local dimension $d\ge2$ \begin{equation*} \mathrm{EoP}_2(W_{+,d})=\log_2\frac{4d(d+1)}{d^2+3d+4}. \end{equation*} We establish additivity for tensor power and, more generally, additivity for finite products of symmetric Werner states with different local dimensions. A canonical purification and its products achieve these values globally, even when arbitrary joint purifications with unrestricted finite dimensional auxiliary systems are allowed. We further examine perturbations away from the symmetric endpoint, and prove the continuity of the optimal value at this endpoint; moreover, we show a sharp square root order of variation in the optimal purity, while the canonical purification remains asymptotically optimal in the achieved entropy as this weight goes to zero.
authors: Shokoufe Faraji

papers.title: Weak-coupling selection and finite-torus entropy in the triangular Ising antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: An antiferromagnetic second-neighbor interaction favors stripe order in the triangular-lattice Ising antiferromagnet, but uniform stripes cannot satisfy odd periodic boundaries. At each fixed odd size $L\geq5$, we minimize this interaction over the ground states of the zero-field nearest-neighbor model on an $L\times L$ torus. We prove a minimum total interface length of $4L$ and classify all $L^2(L^2-1)/2$ selected states. Under the uniform measure on these states, the area fractions of the three stripe orientations approach a uniform distribution over all nonnegative triples summing to one. Thus selection reduces an exponential degeneracy to polynomial growth, while the whole-sample orientation fractions remain broadly distributed. We also derive explicit two-sided entropy-density bounds for periodic spin ground states and honeycomb dimer coverings on $M\times N$ tori, where $M,N$ are the periods along the two primitive lattice directions. For all $M,N\geq3$, the errors relative to the bulk residual entropy are bounded by explicit constants times $\min(M,N)^{-2}$, without an aspect-ratio restriction. These bounds give finite-size accuracy guarantees and control the exponentially small fraction of unperturbed ground states that survive the selection.
authors: Weiqi Jiang, Pengcheng Hou

papers.title: The Devil Went Down to de Sitter: Divergent Effective Field Theory Expansions in Cosmology
papers.abstract: Effective field theories (EFTs) in de Sitter space, and in accelerating cosmologies more generally, must capture phenomena absent in flat space, most notably long-range correlations generated by spontaneous particle production. When heavy physics is integrated out in such time-dependent backgrounds, these effects leave an imprint on the EFT expansion: even at tree level, this is generically an asymptotic rather than convergent series. This is not a failure of EFT. The large-order behavior of the expansion coefficients encodes physical information inaccessible at any finite order, so cosmological EFTs contain hidden data. Using resurgence analysis, we show how this information can be systematically extracted to recover exact and non-perturbative predictions from the perturbative expansion. In the example we study, the resurgent completion is naturally organized in terms of the de Sitter $S$-matrix. This leads us to conjecture a prescription for extracting $S$-matrix data from cosmological EFTs in general. The framework extends to any setting where particle production, or a similar non-perturbative phenomenon, renders the EFT expansion asymptotic. A longer companion paper will provide a more detailed and pedagogical treatment.
authors: Daniele Dorigoni, Laura Engelbrecht, Nadine Nussbaumer, Guilherme L. Pimentel

papers.title: Heavy quarkonium dynamics beyond the binding energy over temperature expansion
papers.abstract: We revisit the pNRQCD open-quantum-system description of bottomonium in a quark-gluon plasma, writing the full master equation in a spherical basis and establishing a framework for its numerical treatment. The equation does not rely on an expansion in the ratio of the binding energy over the temperature, while retaining the Born, Markov, and dilute approximations. It depends on suitable convolutions of Coulombic Green's functions with real-time chromoelectric correlators, rather than a finite set of transport coefficients. It contains jump-operator contributions that enter with both positive and negative signs, so it is not of a Lindblad type. We utilize optimal operator rotations to minimize the negative sector and define a positive-sector approximation that retains only the optimized positive terms, obtaining in this way a Lindblad equation that can be simulated efficiently with the open-source code QTraj for arbitrary chromoelectric spectral functions. We treat the discarded sector as a systematic uncertainty associated with positivity-breaking effects of the pseudo-Lindblad generator. Positivity breaking effects can be attributed to the approximations made in the derivation of the quarkonium master equation, such as the Born--Markov approximations. Using a spectral model constrained by known infrared and ultraviolet limits, we compute the in-medium width and Bjorken-evolved survival probabilities of the $\Upsilon(1\mathrm{S},2\mathrm{S},3\mathrm{S})$. The computations show the convergence of the binding-energy-over-temperature expansion at high temperatures and provide the first large-scale quantum-trajectory simulation results for bottomonium in the low temperature regime. We can thus follow the bottomonium evolution over the full temperature range relevant in heavy-ion collisions.
authors: Nora Brambilla, Arthur Yi-Ting Lin, Tom Magorsch, Antonio Vairo

papers.title: Non-Invertible Charges for M-Theory
papers.abstract: The gauge charges of M-theory M2 and M5 branes almost resemble the charges of a 6-group. The charges of such a 6-group are expected to be modeled by operators with non-invertible fusion. We here consider non-invertible charge defects for continuous 2-groups and 6-groups, aiming to capture the gauge charges of M2 and M5 branes. We find a model for charges of a "pseudo 6-group" $\frak{G}$ which possesses remarkable similarities with known features of M2 and M5 branes, including: Hanany-Witten moves, the $\frak{a}_{N-1}$ charges, higher-form symmetry, and singleton decomposition of M5-brane worldvolume theories, and couplings of M5/anti-M5 states.
authors: Kenneth Intriligator, Aiden Sheckler, Eric Y. Yang

papers.title: The Multi-trace Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
papers.abstract: We introduce a multi-trace eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, an extension of ETH that governs connected correlations of operator matrix elements with arbitrary index structures, including several disjoint index cycles. We derive multi-trace ETH from local rotational invariance, relate its independent data to higher-order free cumulants, and construct a cyclic matrix model that encodes the resulting multi-cycle data. We provide evidence for multi-trace ETH in chaotic quantum systems and compute multi-trace correlations in low-dimensional gravity. In few-body systems, multi-trace contributions arise from correlated periodic orbits, including a linear ramp contribution to the one-point spectral form factor. In two dimensions, we compute interaction-induced multi-trace correlations from a quartically coupled bulk scalar in JT gravity, relating winding matter diagrams to corrections of matter-channel weights and anomalous dimensions. In three dimensions, we show that multi-trace non-Gaussianities arise from both topology-changing saddles and light matter. Using Virasoro TQFT and conformal mean-field theory, we compute examples involving knot and link complements and torus wormholes with matter loops. Across these settings, multi-trace ETH provides a common framework for both connected correlators in chaotic quantum systems and multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes in gravity.
authors: Ahmed I. Abdalla, Gabriele Di Ubaldo, Elisa Tabor

papers.title: Quantum simulation of real-time Yukawa dynamics with qubits and qumodes
papers.abstract: Real-time quantum simulation of field theories offers access to scattering and decay dynamics, circumventing the limitations of Euclidean lattice methods. However, representing bosonic fields on qubits requires a finite-dimensional approximation and can entail costly multi-qubit operations. Hybrid qubit-qumode architectures avoid this by encoding bosonic fields directly in oscillators. We formulate scattering in the (1+1)-dimensional Yukawa theory for such a device, with staggered fermions on qubits and the scalar on qumodes. Trapped ions are a natural candidate, with the fermions on the internal states of the ions and the scalar on their collective motion, so that the Yukawa coupling becomes a native spin-dependent displacement. Emulating the device with tensor networks, we study the decay of a single scalar particle and fermion-antifermion scattering around the resonance region, using observables that can be measured on the device natively. We compare the results with those obtained using lattice perturbation theory. The emulation is able to resolve corrections beyond the Dyson summation of the one-loop self-energy.
authors: Jack Y. Araz, Jeffrey Forshaw, Ross Jenkinson

papers.title: Exhaustive Construction of Generalized Parent Hamiltonians for Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Characterizing local Hamiltonians that host interesting many-body states as eigenstates has been an important problem in quantum many-body physics. For matrix product states (MPS), there is a well-known construction of parent Hamiltonians that have the MPS as the frustration-free ground state. However, recent results on quantum many-body scars have shown that such a construction does not exhaust all possible Hamiltonians that have the MPS as an eigenstate. In this work, we develop an exhaustive construction of generalized parent Hamiltonians that have a given translation-invariant MPS as an eigenstate. These go beyond the conventional projector-based construction of frustration-free parent Hamiltonians, where each local Hermitian term has the MPS as an eigenstate, by allowing non-Hermitian telescoping terms that cancel out with periodic boundary conditions (PBC). We derive a local tensor equation that establishes a correspondence between inequivalent classes of generalized parent Hamiltonians, i.e., those that cannot be related using linear combinations with frustration-free Hamiltonians, and the MPS transfer matrix spectrum. We illustrate the connection to intrinsic physical properties, including non-Abelian symmetries and zero correlation length, and further extend this construction to block-injective MPS. Our framework hence provides a systematic bridge between generalized parent Hamiltonians and the local structure of quantum states.
authors: He-Ran Wang, Lorenzo Gotta, Sanjay Moudgalya

papers.title: Generalized Toric Threefolds from Scattering Diagrams and Broken Lines
papers.abstract: We present an explicit and practical description of Generalized Toric Calabi--Yau threefolds, which are associated with five-brane webs ending on seven-branes, using scattering diagrams and broken lines, based on ideas from arXiv:2410.04714 [hep-th]. Local theta-function algebras and their transition maps give explicit affine charts for opened (resolved) webs, extending familiar toric constructions to non-toric situations. We give a physical interpretation of the deformation parameters, in the case of one or several 7-branes, and deduce behavior under Hanany-Witten transitions and changes of tesselation.
authors: Antoine Bourget, Ignacio Carre\~no Bolla, Quentin Lamouret

papers.title: An obstruction to generalised discrete torsion in string theory
papers.abstract: We reconsider the possibility of turning on generalised discrete torsion in orbifold compactifications, whereby different discrete torsion phases are attached to different fixed points of a given twisted sector. By an explicit inspection of the genus one and genus two vacuum amplitudes for the $T^6/\mathbb{Z}_2^2$ and $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ cases, we show that this is not possible in String Theory. In fact, this generalised discrete torsion, although modular invariant at genus one, leads to an inconsistent interpretation of the spectrum which, in turn, implies a loss of modular invariance on genus-two Riemann surfaces. Our finding is in agreement with a recent classification of allowed topological deformations in equivariant cohomology, which does not include this possibility.
authors: Carlo Angelantonj, Giorgio Leone, Diego Perugini

papers.title: The pinning-field line defect at finite temperature
papers.abstract: We study the pinning-field line defect in the critical $\mathrm{O}(N)$ model at finite temperature, describing a static symmetry-breaking impurity at a quantum critical point. Using the operator product expansion (OPE), analyticity, and thermal periodicity, we construct a manifestly periodic expansion relating heavy-operator asymptotics to low-lying thermal OPE data. We determine thermal correlators and one-point coefficients in the $\varepsilon$-expansion and, combining these results with the two-dimensional Ising endpoint, obtain the Pad\'e estimate $\langle \hat{\phi} \rangle \sim 1.701/\beta^{\smash{\hat{\Delta}_{\smash{\hat{\phi}}}}}$ for the lowest defect operator in the three-dimensional Ising model. We conjecture that truncating the periodic OPE to a few low-lying operators accurately approximates defect correlators. To test this, we numerically solve the large-$N$ thermal saddle and extract defect one-point coefficients across $2<d<4$. In three dimensions, we compute the tilt and longitudinal singlet two-point functions, finding very good agreement with the periodic OPE truncated to the identity and lowest singlet. Finally, we extend the analysis to finite spatial volume using antipodal defects on the sphere.
authors: Julien Barrat, Simone Giombi

papers.title: A local action for Kodaira--Spencer gravity
papers.abstract: A local action is given for Kodaira--Spencer gravity by solving a constraint on the complex structure deformation of a Calabi--Yau threefold in terms of a $(1,1)$ form as the new gravity field. The gauge algebra becomes a genuine $L_{\infty}$ algebra based on a Courant algebroid, while the gravity field and its linearized gauge transformations coincide with those of double field theory. On a real three-dimensional slice, the free action reduces to the Fierz--Pauli action for massless spin-2 plus the Kalb--Ramond action for a B-field. Non-linearly, the theory carries parity-odd interactions with three derivatives, and it is gauge invariant without a level-matching constraint, in this sense defining an unconstrained double field theory. The full theory is encoded in a cyclic $L_{\infty}$ algebra, for which a double copy interpretation is given.
authors: Olaf Hohm

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Hadronization: From String Breaking to Event Generation
papers.abstract: High-energy collisions produce large numbers of quarks and gluons that are bound into hadrons by the confining interactions of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). This hadronization process is intrinsically real-time and non-perturbative. Event generators describe hadronization using phenomenological models with parameters fitted to data rather than calculated from QCD. Uncertainties in these models limit the precision of certain measurements at the Large Hadron Collider. Quantum computers could enable first-principles simulations of these dynamics. Existing quantum simulations of gauge theories have demonstrated string-breaking dynamics. This white paper summarizes the conclusions of the InQubator for Quantum Simulation workshop \textit{From String Dynamics to Event Generation with Quantum Simulation}. We develop a roadmap for extending these simulations to inform phenomenological models of hadronization. A sequence of toy models is proposed for connecting current quantum simulations to QCD. The observables that should be extracted are listed, and the challenges that separate present simulations from quantitative predictions are identified. We propose a staged program in which quantum simulations first provide qualitative modifications to event generators and later provide quantitative input.
authors: Christian W. Bauer, Anthony N. Ciavarella, Jad C. Halimeh, Yannick Meurice, Stephen Mrenna, Martin J. Savage, Giovanni Cataldi, Henry Froland, Dorota M. Grabowska, Sebastian Grieninger, Kenneth Heitritter, Michael Hite, Marc Illa, Saurabh V. Kadam, Henry Lamm, Zhiyao Li, Zane Ozzello, Vincent R. Pascuzzi, Blake Senseman, Kaidi Xu, Xiaojun Yao, Nikita A. Zemlevskiy

papers.title: Interacting scalar-fermion two-component dark matter in a gauged $\boldsymbol{U(1)_{B-L}}$ model
papers.abstract: We propose an interacting two-component dark matter model based on a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model, which also accommodates neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism. The dark sector consists of a Dirac fermion $\chi$ and a complex scalar $S$, which can both be stable without imposing an additional discrete symmetry and are directly coupled by a gauge-invariant Yukawa interaction. The resulting conversion, semi-conversion, and semi-annihilation processes lead to a genuinely coupled freeze-out. After imposing collider and dark matter constraints, we identify viable solutions away from the $Z'$ resonance for both mass hierarchies, $m_S > m_\chi$ and $m_S < m_\chi$. Despite the strong direct-detection constraints, part of the surviving parameter space remains within the reach of next-generation experiments.
authors: Jacinto P. Neto, Farinaldo S. Queiroz, Carlos E. Yaguna

papers.title: Distance to integrability and complexity
papers.abstract: We consider nearest-neighbour interactions on spin-1/2 chains. We find the full set of integrable models of this form and apply a numerical algorithm to determine the "closest" integrable model for a given Hamiltonian. This allows us to define a model-independent distance to integrability. We show that standard measures of chaos interpolate between integrable and chaotic values with increasing values of this distance. However, there is a large variation across models and the distance to integrability provides additional information not directly provided by these diagnostics.
authors: Sean Casey, Marius de Leeuw, Tristan McLoughlin, Sergiy Zhuk

papers.title: Reconstructing string dualities through symmetries of moduli spaces
papers.abstract: We perform a bottom-up analysis of the possible duality descriptions characterizing the perturbative regimes associated to the asymptotic regions of quantum gravity moduli spaces. Our approach relies on the symmetries of such moduli spaces as scalar manifolds, as well as the Emergent String Conjecture, which constrains the possible towers of states becoming light, and thus the interpretation of the dual theories emerging at infinite distance. For supergravity theories with 32 and 16 supercharges, our reconstruction uniquely matches those duality frames associated to top-down toroidal compactifications of M-theory/Type II string theory and heterotic string theory, respectively. For theories with less supersymmetry, moduli spaces exhibit fewer symmetries, and quantum corrections can render certain directions of the classical moduli space inaccessible; nonetheless, we are still able to constrain the possible arrangements of dualities. While these are mostly realized by known top-down constructions, there are some intriguing additional possibilities which might lay in unexplored corners of the string landscape.
authors: Ignacio Ruiz, Germ\'an Varona

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks and their classical surrogates on long-range strongly correlated models
papers.abstract: We benchmark quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) and their classical surrogates for phase differentiation in one-dimensional strongly correlated systems with beyond-nearest-neighbour terms. Using an anisotropic Heisenberg spin chain and an extended $t$-$t'$ Fermi-Hubbard model as representative spin and fermionic testbeds, we train QCNN classifiers on labelled ground-state datasets and map out finite-size phase diagrams. In hybrid setups, we employ Pauli backpropagation to express the QCNN measurement as a weighted sum of Pauli-string expectation values to be evaluated directly on input states, and study how truncation parameters control the trade-off between approximation accuracy and the size of the resulting Pauli expansion. Robust convergence is achieved for the Heisenberg model under aggressive truncation, whereas the Fermi-Hubbard model requires substantially looser thresholds, resulting in a sharp growth in retained Pauli strings and evaluation cost. Our results contribute to charting where hybrid quantum-classical training is viable for learning strongly correlated quantum states, and provide practical guidance for choosing truncation regimes in Pauli backpropagation-based surrogates.
authors: Tatiana A. Bespalova, R\'eka Schwengelbeck, Laura Mismetti, Johannes Schachenmayer, Ivano Tavernelli, Francesco Tacchino

papers.title: A microscopic stochastic field theory for nonlinear pomeron--odderon evolution based on a Doi--Peliti framework
papers.abstract: We construct a reaction-based microscopic realisation of nonlinear pomeron--odderon evolution in rapidity and impact-parameter space. Using the Doi--Peliti formalism, we derive the master equations, their operator representation, the exact hierarchy of factorial moments, and the coherent-state functional integral. The construction admits normalised complex configuration weights while retaining the algebraic conservation law of the gain--loss generator. Pomeron branching and merging yield the complex logistic equation \cite{Kohara:2026} under mean-field factorisation. Pomeron-catalysed odderon branching and ternary odderon fusion provide an odd sector whose evolution is driven by the pomeron background. Without transverse diffusion, the resulting equations admit an analytical solution in quadrature, allowing us to examine amplification, phase evolution, and nonlinear regulation. A specified matching between the first moments and the even and odd scattering profiles connects this evolution to elastic-scattering observables. Illustrative initial conditions produce a nonmonotonic forward ratio and a splitting between the $pp$ and $p\bar p$ channels, while the interference near a diffractive minimum remains sensitive to the relative phases and transverse profiles. These examples illustrate the effective dynamics without constituting a fit to data or a general proof of scattering unitarity.
authors: Anderson Kendi Kohara

papers.title: Triple descent in quantum linear regression
papers.abstract: Quantum linear regression models, such as quantum extreme learning machines and quantum fidelity kernels, are trained on features that can only be estimated from finitely many measurement shots. Sampling noise is usually treated as a nuisance that more shots suppress; we show instead that it can fundamentally reshape the instabilities of the learning problem. As the number of measurement outcomes grows, the prediction error displays a triple-descent profile, with two peaks of fundamentally different origins. The first, classical, peak occurs when the measurement first becomes informationally complete, is a direct analogue of double descent in classical linear regression, and is caused by ill-conditioning of the measurement itself. This peak affects predictions only through their variance, and is thus suppressed by increasing the number of shots at inference. The second, quantum, peak occurs beyond informational completeness when the number of outcomes matches the number of training states: shot noise populates unphysical outcome combinations and the regression fits these pure-noise features with large weights, corrupting the learned model itself. More training or test shots cannot remove this quantum peak, which disappears only in the ideal limit of exact training features. Using random-matrix theory, we derive the shape of both peaks analytically, accounting also for ridge regularization. Our results show that treating quantum features as exactly known overestimates classical instabilities while missing genuinely quantum ones.
authors: Gabriele Lo Monaco, Salvatore Lorenzo, Alessandro Ferraro, Mauro Paternostro, G. Massimo Palma, Luca Innocenti

papers.title: Finesse evolution in a bichromatic cavity under blue and red resonant illumination in vacuum
papers.abstract: The long-term performance of high-finesse optical cavities depends on the stability of their mirror coatings under vacuum and under continuous exposure to high circulating power. In cavities supporting multiple wavelengths, a central question is whether degradation at one wavelength compromises performance at another. Understanding this interplay is essential for those cavity quantum electrodynamics experiments that need diverse optical fields for cavity stabilization, trapping, and light--matter coupling. Here, we investigate wavelength-dependent degradation and recovery of a bichromatic cavity with high-reflectivity coating at 455 nm and 671 nm in vacuum. Cavity ring-down measurements reveal a decrease in the 455 nm finesse from 7.7*10^3 to 1.9*10^3 after 11 hours of continuous exposure to high circulating power. Simultaneous measurements show no measurable degradation at 671 nm. Continuous operation at 671 nm, instead, produces no measurable degradation at either wavelength under the tested conditions. Comparison of oxygen depletion and Avrami-type loss models indicates kinetics compatible with nucleation and growth, without uniquely identifying the microscopic mechanism. We demonstrate partial recovery of the finesse with illumination at 455 nm in air. Our results indicate a wavelength dependence of laser-induced optical damage in bichromatic cavities and provide an estimate of the blue light intensity that can be safely used in such cavities.
authors: M. S. Caracas Nu\~nez, A. Kadakkavattathu, G. Gatta, L. Duca, N. Mizukami, C. Sias

papers.title: Phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave-packet structures in the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We study the phase-space dynamics and multicomponent wave-packet structures of the Dunkl anharmonic oscillator (Kerr medium). Starting from the time-evolved state, we derive analytical expressions for the Dunkl-Husimi $Q$-function and a normalized angular Husimi profile. The Dunkl parameter modifies the coherent-state excitation weights and the parity-dependent phase accumulation, producing angular anisotropy and asymmetric phase-space separation. For the half-integer deformation $\mu=0.5$, the dynamics generate asymmetric multicomponent Husimi patterns with unequal peak heights and an early reconstruction at $t=\pi/\lambda$. For the deformation $\mu=1.0$, the Husimi distribution exhibits broadening while retaining its multimodal structure and unitary evolution. At the fundamental nonlinear revival time, the wave packet is reconstructed for the selected parameter ratio. The standard Kerr dynamics are recovered in the limit $\mu\rightarrow 0$.
authors: D. Ojeda-Guill\'en, R. D. Mota

papers.title: Application a quantum machine learning algorithm to the applied problem of modeling the thermal regime of a servers
papers.abstract: Quantum computing is a rapidly developed field of science. In the NISC era, quantum machine learning stands out, potentially outperforming classical machine learning. In this paper, we explore the applicability of quantum machine learning to a real-world application. We solved the problem of prediction of the temperature of GPUs in a high-performance computing cluster. We trained a quantum circuit to predict the temperature of each of the eight GPU of each cluster node based on 16 physical parameters. We demonstrated that quantum machine learning performs on this task just as well as classical machine learning. Furthermore, using model problems, we demonstrated that quantum machine learning can potentially outperform classical machine learning.
authors: P. V. Buzin, M. A. Remnev

papers.title: Zero mode, Zero influence: Spatial-derivative coupling in particle detectors
papers.abstract: It is common in particle detector models in cavity QED to often omit zero modes or assume their state, compromising causality or introducing ambiguity in their predictions. We show that spatial-derivative coupling eliminates both problems. For free massless scalar fields in static periodic or Neumann cavities of any spatial dimension, cavity-frame spatial derivatives annihilate the zero-mode operator while preserving microcausality. Detector dynamics and entanglement harvesting then depend only on the reduced detector-oscillator state, nonperturbatively and even with initial correlations with the zero mode. Time derivatives and moving-detector rest-frame spatial derivatives can retain zero-mode state dependence not compromising causality. Realized through current coupling in superconducting circuits, spatial-derivative coupling thus makes zero-mode state assumptions unnecessary.
authors: Eduardo Mart\'{i}n-Mart\'{i}nez, Ireneo James Membrere, Adam Teixid\'{o}-Bonfill

papers.title: Painlev\'e VI superintegrability and Heun-Racah algebras
papers.abstract: We study the two fourth-order quantum superintegrable systems in the Euclidean plane that separate in polar coordinates and whose angular potentials are determined by the general four-parameter sixth Painlev\'e transcendent. One system has an oscillator radial term and the other an extended-Coulomb radial term. For both systems we give the fourth-order quantum integral explicitly, derive the cubic symmetry algebra and its Casimir, and construct a deformed-oscillator realization. At fixed energy the two algebras are specializations of the Heun--Racah algebra. Their structure functions contain the same quartic angular factor, determined by the Painlev\'e~VI parameters, while different radial factors distinguish oscillator and Coulomb dynamics. The Coulomb integral is obtained by transforming the Cartesian Hermitian symmetry at the operator level. The lower-order terms generated by the polar coordinate change are essential for commutation with the Hamiltonian. The two quantum systems are also related by the Levi-Civita transformation and coupling-constant metamorphosis, which gives a direct correspondence between their Painlev\'e parameters, algebras, Casimirs and representations. Earlier exceptional-Jacobi models arise at special rational parameter values, whereas the results here apply to the full four-parameter Painlev\'e~VI family. We also compare the quantum results with the corresponding classical Poisson algebras.
authors: Ian Marquette, Sarah Post

papers.title: Quantum superposition of Cosmic String spacetimes
papers.abstract: Since the quantum nature of spacetime is anticipated by a theory of Quantum Gravity, the possibility of spacetime superposition would be a natural consequence. This spacetime interference phenomena could bring us some clues about what effects could be expected over quantum fields and their interaction with matter. In this article, we investigate the effect of the superposition of a Cosmic String spacetime on the Unruh-De Witt detector. This is of interest as the spacetimes possess flat geometry but non-trivial topology. We analyze the effect of the interference of a Cosmic String with different topological charge over the Unruh-De Witt detector response function to vacuum fluctuations. We obtain some quantum interference effects, due to the superposition of spacetimes, which would be absent if a classical probabilistic mixture of spacetimes would be considered. In this manner, we obtain real physical consequences that would be indications of a Quantum Gravity phenomena.
authors: Enrique Arias, Shoshauna Gauvin, Willy Izquierdo, Robert B. Mann

papers.title: A Koszul-Type Splitting Theorem for Complex Supermanifolds
papers.abstract: We study the splitting problem for complex supermanifolds using formal exponential maps and Ehresmann connections. We show that every formal exponential map induces a splitting of the underlying supermanifold. Furthermore, we establish that every Ehresmann connection determines a linearization of the infinite jet space, extending the corresponding construction for ordinary manifolds to supermanifolds. For Ehresmann connections preserving the zero section, we construct a formal exponential map in two ways: via the linearization of the infinite jet space and directly from the connection operator. We prove that both constructions yield the same map and induce the same splitting, thereby generalizing Koszul's splitting theorem from linear connections to zero-section-preserving Ehresmann connections. Finally, we provide examples showing that, without this assumption, the two constructions may yield different splittings, or one or both of them may fail to induce a splitting.
authors: Luiz F. A. Campos, Alexey Sharapov, Elizaveta Vishnyakova

papers.title: Stability of Solitons in the Parametrically Driven and Damped Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation in Arbitrary Dimension
papers.abstract: We study the spectral stability of soliton solutions of the parametrically driven and damped nonlinear Schr\"odinger (PDDNLS) equation with power-law nonlinearity $|\Psi|^{2\kappa}\Psi$ in $N$ dimensions. We identify two families of stationary solutions, $\Psi_\pm$, whose existence is determined by two conditions: one involving the nonlinearity exponent~$\kappa$ and the spatial dimension~$N$, and another involving the forcing amplitude~$r$ and the damping coefficient~$\rho$. By linearising around these solutions and introducing a convenient parametrisation through~$\varepsilon$, we reduce the stability problem to a dissipationless eigenvalue problem for two Schr\"odinger-type operators, $L_0$ and $L_1$. We prove that $\Psi_-$ is always unstable, while for $\Psi_+$, we carry out a complete spectral analysis by decomposing the problem into angular momentum sectors $\mathcal{S}_l$. We show that modes with $l \geq 2$ generate no instabilities and that no complex quadruplets arise on~$\mathcal{S}_1$. We also derive an analytical instability criterion on $\mathcal{S}_l$ by combining a Vakhitov--Kolokolov-type argument with a local analysis that determines the direction of the eigenvalue splitting near the origin. In addition, we uncover new phenomena at both small and large values of $\kappa$ that were not investigated in earlier one-dimensional studies. Numerical stability diagrams for $N = 1, 2, 3$ are presented.
authors: Fernando Carre\~no-Navas

papers.title: Recurrence in Sequence Space: How Epistasis Mimics Shared Ancestry
papers.abstract: Sequences in a protein family do not explore the sequence space freely: folding, packing, and binding couple residues, so the set of viable sequences is irreducibly correlated, a phenomenon referred to as epistasis. We show that such correlations lower the \emph{intrinsic dimension} $d_{\rm IN}$ of sequence space, counteracting the concentration of measure and broadening the distribution of pairwise distances. Consequentially, they make it likely that independently evolving lineages \emph{recur}, approaching one another by chance long after they last shared an ancestor. Using Kac's lemma we show that the logarithmic mean recurrence time grows linearly with the intrinsic dimension, $\log \tau_{\rm rec} \propto {d_{\rm IN}}$ for typical sequences, so strongly constrained (low-dimensional) families recur often and generate sequence similarity that carries no genealogical signal. We establish this first in a solvable Ising-like model with tunable correlation, then in a real protein family using Potts models and Markov chain Monte Carlo, where $d_{\rm IN}$ remains predictive of recurrence even in multi-basins landscapes. Because recurrence is a property of the evolutionary process rather than of any estimator, it bounds the recoverability of deep history for distance-based and likelihood methods alike.
authors: Pietro Chiarantoni, Mina Mahboubi, Jason Lamanna, Vincenzo Carnevale

papers.title: 5d SCFTs and Intersection Theory of Generalized Toric Threefolds
papers.abstract: Five-dimensional superconformal field theories are intrinsically strongly coupled fixed points that can be realized as M-theory on local Calabi-Yau threefolds with canonical singularities. The low-energy effective theory on their extended Coulomb branch is governed by a cubic prepotential, determined by the triple intersection numbers of divisors in the resolved geometry. For toric threefolds, dual to 5-brane webs, these numbers are computed combinatorially from the toric polygon. However, no such description has been available for generalized toric polygons (GTPs), dual to 5-brane webs with 7-branes, since the corresponding generalized toric Calabi-Yau threefolds are generally non-toric. We show that the 7-brane data are encoded by additional lines in the GTP, which correspond to non-toric, non-compact divisors that we call exuberant divisors. Building on a local analysis of these divisors and on the associativity of the intersection product, we develop an algorithm that computes the triple intersection numbers, and hence the prepotential, directly from the combinatorial data of the GTP. We illustrate it in examples and provide a Mathematica code implementation of the intersection algorithm.
authors: H\"ulya Arg\"uz, Antoine Bourget, Pierrick Bousseau, Julius F. Grimminger, Sakura Schafer-Nameki

papers.title: Oscillatory instability of subcritical stationary solutions in the parametrically driven, damped nonlinear Dirac equation
papers.abstract: The dynamics of the nonlinear Dirac equation (NLDE) under the influence of dissipation and parametric forcing exhibit complex phenomenologies, including soliton destruction and chaotic transitions, which have been extensively observed in numerical simulations. However, a rigorous analytical understanding of the underlying instability mechanisms in the subcritical regime has remained open. In this work, we provide a theoretical answer to these numerical findings by establishing the spectral instability of the fundamental soliton solution. Our methodology relies on a three-step approach linking local asymptotic analyses with global topological arguments. First, we characterize the generalized null space at the critical parameter ($\lambda_c$), revealing the onset of instability through the splitting of the zero eigenvalue within a parity-dependent subspace. Second, in the non-relativistic limit ($\lambda \to 0$), we use a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction to reduce the linearized Dirac's operators into a P\"oschl--Teller Schr\"odinger operator, thereby identifying the instability source as a unique real pair of discrete eigenvalues in the restricted problem. Third, we extend these local results to the entire subcritical domain using a topological continuation argument, which tracks the invariance of the spectral parity in a subset of the complex plane. These analytical results rigorously confirm the instability of the soliton, providing the mathematical mechanism for the wave collapse observed in the driven-damped system.
authors: Fernando Carre\~no-Navas

papers.title: Non-Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics of Glass-Forming Liquids under Continuous Cooling: Microscopic Inner Clocks, Fictive Temperatures, and Kauzmann Diagrams
papers.abstract: The description of macroscopic properties in out-of-equilibrium amorphous solids such as gels and glasses, typically processed under finite cooling rates, remains a fundamental challenge for modern statistical physics. In this work, we employ the Non-Equilibrium Self-Consistent Generalized Langevin Equation (NESCGLE) theory to construct a microscopic description of the structural and calorimetric glass transition under continuous cooling. Building upon the microscopic Onsager-Machlup interpretation of Narayanaswamy's material time (the inner clock $u(t)$) [J.Chem.Phys. 156, 244506 (2022)], we recover Tool's fictive temperature $T_f$ directly from the evolving spatial pair correlations and show that wavenumber dispersion naturally generalizes the classical scalar $T_f$ into a continuous mode spectrum governed by de Gennes narrowing at the primary cage peak. Across wide variations in cooling rate down to the quasi-static limit, the theory yields first-principles non-equilibrium Kauzmann diagrams for the two-body excess entropy that dynamically avert the Kauzmann crisis above the ideal dynamic arrest temperature $T_c$, while predicting sigmoidal relaxational heat-capacity steps consistent with computer simulations and calorimetry. Finally, we extract the cooling-rate-dependent glass transition temperature $T_g(q)$ from both equal-area integrals and differential heat-capacity landmarks, demonstrating that its asymptotic approach toward $T_c$ obeys a critical power-law scaling governed directly by the equilibrium dynamic arrest exponent.
authors: R. Peredo-Ortiz, M. Medina-Noyola, L. F. Elizondo-Aguilera

papers.title: On the properties of the potential and the spherical harmonic expansions for general planets
papers.abstract: The convergence of spherical harmonic expansions (SHEs) of gravitational potentials below the Brillouin sphere has been a long-standing problem in potential theory and geodesy. In previous work, some of the present authors gave a necessary and sufficient condition for convergence along a fixed ray, formulated in terms of analyticity of a longitudinal average of the balayage density. In the present paper, we extend these results to arbitrary physical solid planets, assuming only that the planet is a compact subset of $\mathbb R^3$ and that its density belongs to $L^\infty$. We establish sharp regularity properties of the gravitational potential at the Brillouin sphere. The potential and its first derivative extend continuously to the sphere, the first derivative is locally H\"older continuous with exponent $1/2$, and the second derivative satisfies the optimal bound $V''(z)=O\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial\mathbb D)^{-1/2}\bigr)$ under nontangential approach from the exterior. We also obtain sharp estimates for the spherical harmonic coefficients: $a_\ell=O(\ell^{-3/2}).$ If, for almost every latitude, the Brillouin sphere is a one-sided Lebesgue point from the interior of the longitudinally averaged density, then $a_\ell=o(\ell^{-3/2}).$ Both estimates are optimal. We explicitly recover the balayage density on the Brillouin sphere from the exterior gravitational potential, and its circular averages from the potential along a single radial line. Finally, we give a physical characterization of convergence of the SHE below the Brillouin sphere. If the SHE converges at such a point, then, after truncating the planet at any suitable intermediate radius, the gravitational potential of the removed outer part is completely determined by that of the remaining truncated planet. This provides a direct interpretation of the strong constraint imposed by convergence below the Brillouin sphere.
authors: Ovidiu Costin, Rodica D. Costin, Marjorie K. Drake, Gerald V. Dunne, Crichton Ogle

papers.title: Metastability of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional Ginzburg--Landau model with pinning
papers.abstract: We study the persistence of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional magnetic Ginzburg--Landau model with a spatially dependent pinning term. Factoring out the equilibrium profile associated with the pinning term reduces the problem to the analysis of a weighted Ginzburg--Landau functional. In the extreme type-II regime, we construct locally minimizing vortexless configurations for applied fields extending far beyond the first critical field. We obtain quantitative estimates showing that these configurations remain close, up to gauge transformations, to a Meissner-type state determined by a weighted London problem. We also prove the uniqueness, up to gauge transformations, of the locally minimizing Meissner-type branch within a quantitatively controlled class of local minimizers. A central difficulty is to derive elliptic estimates that remain uniform in the Ginzburg--Landau parameter in the presence of the resulting spatially dependent weight. Under a small-BMO assumption on this weight, we obtain the required regularity and extend to the three-dimensional pinned setting the metastability picture previously established for the homogeneous model.
authors: Carlos Rom\'an

papers.title: VESPER: Online Learning of Free Energies with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective
papers.abstract: Computing molecular free-energy landscapes over collective variables (CVs) is central to understanding molecular mechanisms, but poses a difficult learning problem without training data available a priori. Samples of the marginal CV distribution must be generated by molecular dynamics (MD), whose trajectories can remain trapped in metastable states and rarely cross the free-energy barriers governing conformational changes or chemical reactions. We introduce VESPER, which couples the generation of these samples to neural-network-driven free-energy learning: MD supplies configurations for learning, while the evolving model biases the MD to accelerate exploration and generate further training data. VESPER minimizes a single variational objective that is convex in the free energy and can combine several tempering levels, each flattening the free-energy landscape to promote barrier crossing. Every level has the same physical free energy as its minimizer, allowing data from all levels to train one shared model without reweighting. Learning uses the difference in mean parameter gradients between biased MD configurations and auxiliary walkers that explore the flattened model in CV space. We prove conditional convergence of the coupled overdamped population dynamics without replica exchange under log-Sobolev and Polyak-Lojasiewicz assumptions. VESPER matches or improves on established enhanced-sampling methods on alanine dipeptide and yields self-consistent free-energy reconstructions from three to six CVs on alanine tetrapeptide. For methane dehydrogenation on Ni(511) with a machine-learned interatomic potential, it recovers two-CV Boltzmann marginals and a reactant-to-saddle free-energy difference along a three-CV path, both qualitatively consistent with the lower-dimensional reference. It also samples RMSD-defined folded and unfolded regions of chignolin while biasing seventeen CVs.
authors: Jay L. Kaplan, Gustavo R. P\'erez-Lemus, Mengjian Hua, Juan J. de Pablo, Eric Vanden-Eijnden

papers.title: Early Fault-Tolerant Magic State Synthesis and Spacetime Efficient Analog Rotations with Color Code on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: With recent improvements to syndrome extraction scheduling and decoding, and the availability of complete transversal Clifford operations and lattice surgery, color code is an especially promising platform for quantum processors with local connectivity. The key ingredient for universal computation is thus generating useful magic states with limited resources. Space-Time Efficient Analog Rotations (STAR) and Fault-tolerant magic state synthesis (MSS) are two such methods for magic state generation, targeted for near-term and long-term quantum computing, respectively. In this work, we perform the first implementations of both magic state paradigms on a superconducting quantum processor. We present a STAR-type injection protocol on the color code, with favorable error rate and spacetime costs versus prior protocols on both the color and surface codes. We then implement a MSS factory by performing multi-patch magic state cultivations, interleaved with transversal Clifford operations, and lattice-surgery magic state teleportation. Under post-selection, we achieve a kickback tomography correct sign probability of $99.9859\%$ on cultivated $T_L$ states, $96\%$ tomographic fidelity on logical analog rotation states, and $91\%$ fidelity on synthesized logical magic states consuming 3 cultivated $T_L$ states, 3 transversal Hadamard operations, and real-time feed-forward $S_L$ corrections during magic state teleportation. We compare the efficacy of post-selection, Most-Likely-Error (MLE) decoding, and concatenated-matching decoding throughout, highlighting the potential of end-to-end color code computation.
authors: Sean Garner, Aaron Hoyt, Shuwen Kan, Samuel Stein, Chenxu Liu, Ang Li

papers.title: Measurement-angle control of a continuously monitored quantum oscillator: purification limits and optimal protocols
papers.abstract: We study the dynamic purification of a continuously monitored quantum harmonic oscillator coupled to a thermal bath, where the control is the quadrature measurement angle of up to two detectors with prescribed strengths and efficiencies. Within the Gaussian regime, the conditional state covariance obeys a deterministic Riccati equation, and we ask what purity can be reached and sustained by manipulating the angle in time, in analogy with rapid-purification protocols for qubits. We propose, analyze, and compare constant-rate, greedy, vibrational, and variational monitoring strategies on the basis of sustained purity starting from the thermal bath state, and quantify to what extent they are able to maintain higher purity levels compared to lab-fixed or phase-locked detectors. We highlight structural features, operational limits, and optimal protocols from each strategy and study how model parameters shape control performance. We observe that in the absence of measurement-frame anisotropy, the time-dependent strategies achieve higher but similar performance. Once this symmetry is broken, their performances diverge, either improving or worsening depending on the relative timescales of oscillator dynamics, thermalization, and measurement.
authors: Ralph Sabbagh, Olga Movilla Miangolarra, Andrew N. Jordan, Tryphon T. Georgiou

papers.title: $^{85}$Rb electromagnetically induced transparency and absorption on two collinear $5S_{1/2}\rightarrow5P_{1/2}\rightarrow5D_{3/2}\rightarrow 25F_{5/2}$ three-photon cascade schemes
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of three-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature Rb vapor. Using the cascade system $5S_{1/2}\rightarrow5P_{1/2}\rightarrow5D_{3/2}\rightarrow 25F_{5/2}$ in $^{85}$Rb, we explore two collinear laser-beam configurations. The detunings of the upper two lasers of the cascade system are varied. In both configurations, the probe transmission maps contain rich sets of EIT/EIA features and substructures. To explain these, we utilize a dressed-atom and a quantum Monte Carlo trajectory method. The latter includes 108 relevant fine- and hyperfine-structure levels and their magnetic substates, accounting for coherent optical drives, optical pumping, atom recycling, electromagnetic decays via the $5P_{J}$ levels, and velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions. We find quantum-trajectory solutions of the Lindblad master equation, which show good agreement with experimental data and aid in finding physical explanations for the observed spectra. To further explore collision-induced spectral features, collisional loss of EIT/EIA visibility, velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions, we acquire spectra in Rb cells with 50 and 500~mTorr of Ar gas. Our work is of interest to studies of multi-level EIT systems that underpin emerging quantum technologies, where accurate accounting of internal atomic structure, laser beam geometry, optical pumping, transit time, and collisional effects is critical.
authors: Shuaijie Li, Alisher Duspayev, Georg Raithel

papers.title: Universality of Large-Scale Geometry For Critical Random-Cluster Models
papers.abstract: The understanding of the behaviour of critical lattice models in two dimensions has made immense progress in the past couple of decades, with conformal invariance as its conjectured end goal. We consider here the critical random-cluster model (or FK-percolation) on a large class of graphs --- namely bi-periodic isoradial graphs --- with cluster-weight~$q \in [1,4]$. Following up on the establishment of rotational invariance at criticality in \cite{Rotation}, we prove that the large scale behaviour of these models is asymptotically the same on all such graphs. These include the critical homogeneous models on the square, triangular and hexagonal lattices.
authors: Ulrik Thinggaard Hansen, Ioan Manolescu

papers.title: Validation of the five-electron pO qubit in Si using full configuration interaction
papers.abstract: The $pO$ qubit is a recently proposed charge qubit consisting of five electrons confined in a gate-defined Si quantum dot. Because its two qubit states have no dipole moment, it couples to electric fields only through the quadrupole moment, suppressing the dominant decoherence channel of conventional charge qubits while retaining all-electrical control. The original proposal was formulated in a shell-filling picture without Coulomb interactions. In this work we perform full configuration interaction (FCI) calculations to assess the impact of the Coulomb interaction on the viability of the $pO$ qubit. We find that the interacting eigenstates occupy orbital shells beyond the shell-filling picture, with the degree of excitation governed by the competition between valley splitting, orbital energy, and Coulomb energy scales. Additionally, we find that the ground states form degenerate doublets, but of two distinct kinds. Above a crossover near a valley splitting of $E_{\rm{VS}}\approx50~\mu$eV the doublet is a pair of orbital angular momentum excitations with $|\langle L_z\rangle|=1$ in the lower valley, while below the crossover the doublet is a pair of single valley excitations with $\langle L_z\rangle=0$. Despite this substantial departure from the shell-filling picture, for $E_{\rm{VS}} > 50~\mu$eV the essential features, vanishing dipole moments and nonzero quadrupole tensor between qubit states are preserved. We show that the vanishing dipole is in fact guaranteed by the symmetry properties of the five-electron Hamiltonian. The same energy scales that govern the orbital occupation also set the quadrupole tensor elements and the first excited state energy gap, both of which are in principle tunable through device engineering.
authors: David W. Kanaar, John H. Caporaletti, J. P. Kestner, Christopher R. Anderson, Mark F. Gyure

papers.title: Multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function
papers.abstract: We construct multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function as nested products of overlap coefficients between eigenfunctions of twisted primitive elements in representations of the modular double of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. The construction is a hyperbolic counterpart of the nested multivariate Askey--Wilson polynomials and functions. Using iterated coproducts, we derive four systems of difference equations for which these multivariate functions are joint eigenfunctions. The four systems correspond to the two sets of variables and the two step sizes $iw_1$ and $iw_2$, which are interchanged by modular duality. We also prove that Ruijsenaars' one-variable transform is unitary in the parameter regime required for the construction, for positive as well as complex conjugate $w_1,w_2$. A two-sided normalization of the kernel separates the input and output weights, so that iterating one-variable transforms yields unitary multivariate transforms with explicit inverse and Plancherel formulas.
authors: Wolter Groenevelt, Rik Ledoux

papers.title: Bilateral Christoffel-Geronimus-Uvarov formulas for mixed-type orthogonality on algebraic supports
papers.abstract: Christoffel-type determinant formulas construct both normalized polynomial families and their reproducing kernel for mixed-type orthogonality in several variables after independent rational matrix transformations on the two arguments. The pairing may have a rectangular matrix of functionals, with separate degree bounds on each component, and may be supported on an algebraic variety. The reduced matrices are calculated from the original biorthogonal polynomials, rational moments, polynomial division and the masses left free by division; their nonvanishing determinants characterize existence and uniqueness. For measure pairings the rational data are expressed by Cauchy and multivariate Fantappie transforms. Exact dimension counts incorporate the four matrix factors and the relations of the support. For normal degree-ordered original families and fixed factors, when the component degrees on each side differ by a bounded amount and the normalization dimension grows at most like one degree layer, the resulting orders are bounded on curves and grow at most linearly on surfaces. For pairings allowing scalar factors to move between arguments, called balanced pairings, an exact obstruction determines whether a bilateral mass decomposes into unilateral masses when the denominators act injectively. Residue duality provides coordinates for division and mass quotients on integral curves, including singular points, and on the finite surface quotients specified here. Explicit singular-curve families retain nondegenerate residue pairings as denominator zeros coalesce. Positive congruences admit a further reduction by orthogonal projection, while balanced pairings give simultaneous intertwining identities for all coordinate multiplication matrices.
authors: Manuel Ma\~nas

papers.title: A Hierarchical direct solver for Lippmann-Schwinger equations based on boundary traces
papers.abstract: A high-order hierarchical direct solver for variable-media scattering in two dimensions is presented. Standard discretizations for these problems produce dense linear systems that are commonly solved iteratively, requiring a new global solve for each incident field. The method proposed here instead constructs a reusable scattering operator for the inhomogeneous medium, based on a hierarchical subdivision of the computational domain. First, high-accuracy leaf scattering operators are built from discretized local integral equations. Up the hierarchy, neighboring boxes are merged to build the scattering operators for successively larger boxes. A key feature of the method is that each scattering operator is represented as a map of incoming traces to outgoing traces. Consequently, volume unknowns appear only in the leaf computations; all higher levels of the hierarchy operate entirely on boundary traces. The hierarchical solver is presented first at the continuum level and discretized only afterward using high-order local volume quadrature, polynomial trace representations, and boundary integral techniques. For a discretization involving $N$ degrees of freedom, the method requires $O(N^{3/2})$ work and $O(N\log N)$ storage to build all scattering operators. Once these are available, any incoming field can be processed at cost $O(N)$ if only the outgoing field is required, and cost $O(N\log N)$ if the full field is required. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy on a range of challenging scattering problems including cavities, back-scattering, limited regularity, and high wavenumber, that pose significant challenges to iterative methods.
authors: Yunhui Cai, Simon Dirckx, Joar Bagge, Per-Gunnar Martinsson

papers.title: A block-encoding approach to the Segawa-Suzuki spectral mapping theorem
papers.abstract: We revisit the Segawa--Suzuki spectral mapping theorem for abstract Szegedy-type quantum walks from a block-encoding viewpoint. Retaining both eigenspaces of the involution underlying the chiral symmetry yields a natural two-by-two block representation in which the usual discriminant operator and its counterpart form the diagonal blocks. The non-endpoint spectral mapping theorem then follows from an elementary Schur decomposition, substantially simplifying the original proof by avoiding its invariant-subspace decomposition and approximate-eigenvector arguments. The same framework establishes the result for the spectrum, point spectrum, and Fredholm essential spectrum and gives a direct block-theoretic description of the endpoint inherited and birth eigenspaces. We illustrate the construction with a one-dimensional split-step quantum walk.
authors: Yohei Tanaka

papers.title: Detector Placement Relaxes Efficiency Requirements for Detecting a Weak Coherent Link
papers.abstract: A weak coherent link can produce unusually early arrivals without changing stationary count rates. Missed jumps along routes available without the link can produce similar records, obscuring its presence. On an eight-site ring, relocating the same detector losses exposes one more crossing on the easiest background route to hide, without changing the dynamics or leading link signal. At fixed error and a common observation-time scaling, the tolerated missed fraction and time-bin width follow fourth-root rather than square-root scaling with link strength. These requirements hold for every decision using the counting record and are met using three event counts per bin, with all elapsed time included. At the same stationary collected flux, where jumps are monitored can therefore determine the time resolution needed for weak-link sensing.
authors: M. H. Yu, S. Y. Li, X. Z. Zhang

papers.title: Optimal Estimation in Weak Value Amplification with a Position Pointer
papers.abstract: We experimentally evaluate five estimators for weak-value amplification (WVA) using a position pointer to measure birefringence time delays. Two general approaches are considered: measuring the position shift $\Delta x$ and measuring the probability change $\Delta P_w$ of successful postselection. Specifically, five estimators are investigated: CCD-detected fringe shift $\Delta x$, quadrant photodiode (PDQ) transversal voltage difference (XDIFF), and lock-in amplifier output phase $\eta$ (for $\Delta x$ measurement), as well as PDQ total output voltage (SUM) and CCD-detected average photon number $N_r$ (for $\Delta P_w$ measurement). The measurement precision is characterized by the Allan deviation over a range of input laser powers $P_0$. Generally, measuring the position shift $\Delta x$ yields higher precision than measuring the probability change $\Delta P_w$. At $P_0=0.5$~mW, corresponding to a laser-power-limited regime, direct measurement of the fringe displacement with the CCD achieves a minimum Allan deviation of $(5.30\pm0.10)\times10^{-3}$~as, approaching the corresponding photon-statistical Cram\'er--Rao bound (CRB). At $P_0=50$~mW, corresponding to a detector-limited regime, PDQ detection combined with lock-in demodulation provides the best precision, reaching $(1.80\pm0.06)\times10^{-3}$~as and remaining close to the corresponding CRB. These results demonstrate that the optimal readout depends on the available optical power, detector dynamic range, and technical noise, providing practical guidance for selecting readout strategies in high-precision WVA-based metrology.
authors: Jing-Hui Huang, Jing Zhang, Jian Ge, Lichao Liu, Wang Luo, Xiang-Yun Hu

papers.title: A closed formula for the Poisson cohomology of scalar Dubrovin-Novikov brackets in arbitrary dimension
papers.abstract: The structure of the Poisson cohomology groups for scalar Poisson brackets of Dubrovin-Novikov type with $D$ independent variables has been first described in arXiv:1512.05744 ; in that work, a complete dimensional counting was provided for $D=2$, and some numerical results exhibited for $D=3$, $D=4$. Here, we prove a formula for the dimensional counting of the Poisson cohomology for arbitrary $D$. Moreover, we show how to obtain canonical representatives for each cohomology class.
authors: Matteo Casati

papers.title: Exact scalarization thresholds and onset laws for a nonminimally coupled scalar field on the Ellis wormhole
papers.abstract: We study a real scalar field nonminimally coupled to curvature on a fixed Ellis wormhole background. The scalar perturbation decouples at linear order, and the substitution $ x=a \tan z $ reduces its static radial equation to a trigonometric P\"oschl-Teller problem. This yields the exact threshold spectrum $ \zeta_{n\ell}=(n+\ell+1)^2/2 $, closed-form Gegenbauer profiles, and an exact count of negative radial eigenvalues in each angular sector. The s-wave thresholds are zero-energy resonances at which the growth rate rises linearly, whereas the $ \ell \geq1\ $ threshold states are square integrable and the growth rate rises as a square root. At the first threshold we also obtain the next-order term, $ \sigma a=(\pi/4)g-(3\pi/16)g^2+O(g^3) $ with $g=2\zeta-1 $. For a probe field with quartic self-interaction, we show that no nontrivial spherical static solution exists for $\zeta\leq1/2 $ and derive local branch expansions near the s-wave thresholds. Numerical evolutions are consistent with saturation on the nodeless branch. These nonlinear results refer to the probe-field model; they do not establish the existence or stability of fully backreacted scalarized wormholes.
authors: Abdullah Guvendi, Omar Mustafa, Claudio Furtado

papers.title: The Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem and Dynamical Love Number in Schwarzschild Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study the real-time response of a Schwarzschild black hole in the Hartle-Hawking state to an external massless scalar field. Using a complexified radial contour to represent the Schwinger-Keldysh closed time path, we describe dissipation, thermal fluctuations and conservative tidal response within a common framework. Before performing tidal matching, we derive the equilibrium fluctuation-dissipation relation directly from the radial construction for every scalar multipole at arbitrary real frequency. In the low-frequency tidal expansion, we recover the known relation between the logarithmic running of the conservative dynamical Love coefficient at order $\omega^2$ and the leading dissipative response at order $\omega$. We explain how the same leading absorptive coefficient enters both relations at low frequency and trace the unit coefficient of the running relation to the Schwarzschild horizon slope. In the Hartle-Hawking state, this common coefficient relates the logarithmic running directly to the zero-frequency thermal noise. Kubo-Martin-Schwinger analyticity determines the thermal noise from the dissipative response, whereas the near-zone radial equation and tidal matching determine the conservative logarithmic running.
authors: Dimitrios Giataganas, Alex Kehagias, Antonio Riotto

papers.title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model
papers.abstract: We study the Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow of the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model, a four-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge theory with chirally invariant four-Fermi interactions, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group~(GFERG). Our gauge-invariant ansatz (truncation) for the 1PI Wilson action keeps a general photon kinetic function~$\mathcal{K}_\tau(k^2)$, the fermion mass, and the scalar and vector four-Fermi couplings. For a fixed gauge coupling~$e^2$, the Gaussian and NJL (quasi-)fixed points on the critical surface merge at~$e_c^2\simeq17$, as anticipated by the ladder Schwinger--Dyson equation and the conventional Wilsonian renormalization group. We then let $e^2$ itself flow. Owing to the manifest gauge invariance of the GFERG, the flow of~$e^2$ is governed solely by the photon anomalous dimension~$\gamma_A$, which remains positive along both branches up to the merging point. Hence, no fixed point with~$e^2\neq0$ exists. Flows from a sufficiently large~$e^2$ in the ultraviolet (UV) reach the chirally broken phase even for vanishing four-Fermi couplings, so the gauge interaction does trigger chiral symmetry breaking. The merging point, however, is not a fixed point, and the gauge coupling vanishes in any continuum limit within our truncation.
authors: Sorato Nagao, Hiroshi Suzuki

papers.title: Ultra-broadband quantum infrared spectroscopy extending to 20 {\textmu}m
papers.abstract: Quantum infrared spectroscopy (QIRS), which exploits quantum interference between photon-pair generation processes, enables infrared spectroscopy using only visible and near-infrared (VNIR) light sources and detectors. Extending the spectral coverage of QIRS into the long-wavelength infrared region up to 20 {\textmu}m is crucial for the identification and characterization of a broad range of materials. However, implementing QIRS beyond 10 {\textmu}m has been challenging because the nonlinear materials used to date do not provide suitable photon-pair sources in this spectral region. Here, we design a wavelength-tunable photon-pair source based on a gallium selenide crystal and develop a QIRS system covering a broad spectral range from 8.6 to 20 {\textmu}m. Using this system, we measure the transmittance spectrum of a polystyrene film and observe characteristic absorption bands beyond 10 {\textmu}m relevant to identifying polystyrene and to probing local chain conformation. These results demonstrate that QIRS is capable of covering the entire molecular fingerprint region.
authors: Yu Mukai, Ryo Okamoto, Shigeki Takeuchi

papers.title: Holonomy classification, gyroscope precession, and Landau levels in G\"odel-type spacetimes and their superfluid analog
papers.abstract: We derive the parallel-transport holonomies of circles centered on the symmetry axis in the homogeneous G\"odel-type family of Rebou\c{c}as and Tiomno, which includes the G\"odel universe, the causal member with $m^2=4\Omega^2$, and the Som--Raychaudhuri limit. The holonomy is governed by a single invariant $\Delta(r)$, whose sign determines whether the Lorentz transformation is elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic. We determine the number of parabolic radii across the family and prove that, whenever the azimuthal circles become closed timelike curves (CTCs), the chronology radius satisfies $\Delta(r_c)=-\cosh(mr_c)<0$. We also express this invariant in terms of Killing-vector scalars, derive the vector and spinor Wilson loops, give the exact condition for trivial holonomy after a finite number of turns, and analyze Fermi--Walker transport on circular CTCs. Finally, we discuss an analogy with the effective metric of a rotating superfluid, valid under stated conditions, and derive exact expressions for the radial $L^2$ localization of Klein--Gordon Landau modes relative to the Som--Raychaudhuri chronology radius. The geometric results are exact within the metric family considered; the discussion of the analog system relies on the validity of a coarse-grained effective description.
authors: Claudio Furtado, G. Q. Garcia, Abdullah Guvendi, Alexandre M. de M. Carvalho

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Parameter Setting in Digitized Counterdiabatic QAOA
papers.abstract: Optimizing parameters separately for each problem instance limits the reuse of variational quantum algorithms. We develop empirical scaling laws for parameter setting in the digitized counterdiabatic quantum approximate optimization algorithm (DC-QAOA) for weighted MaxCut. The prescription combines exact covariance under uniform edge-weight rescaling with power laws in mean degree fitted separately to offline-optimized cost and counterdiabatic angles. After the weight and degree scales are removed, the optimized angles of different training graphs cluster around common amplitudes, so a small coefficient table suffices. Frozen coefficients assign angles from a target graph's mean degree and root-mean-square edge weight without target-instance variational optimization. In ideal-circuit simulations across 1050 test graphs spanning ten graph families and five positive edge-weight distributions, mean optimal-solution probability is higher than that of the fixed-angle quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) at each depth from one to four layers, reaching 19.36% versus 13.11% at four layers. A six-layer extension on 600 graphs also shows a mean probability advantage. Hardware execution on the IBM Quantum processor ibm_fez for 21 unit-weight 3-regular graphs shows a mean probability advantage at one layer, while the ordering reverses at two layers. In separate energy-based experiments, direct assignment gives a higher mean approximation ratio than random-start optimization reaches within 500 evaluations, and refinement started from the formula angles improves it further. These results show how a scaling-based representation of optimized angles can guide parameter reuse across graph instances, enabling direct parameter assignment without target-instance variational optimization and providing initial angles for local refinement.
authors: Yaocheng Chen, Jiapei Zhuang

papers.title: Quantum Diffusion and the Block-Size Crossover in the Block Anderson Model
papers.abstract: We study the block Anderson Hamiltonian \(H_L=\lambda\Psi_L+\mathcal V\) on the discrete torus \((\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d\), \(d\geq2\), where \(\Psi_L\) is the nearest-neighbor Laplacian and \(\mathcal V\) consists of independent \(W^d\times W^d\) GOE blocks. In the weak-disorder limit \(\lambda\to\infty\), we establish an entrywise local law, a spatial scaling limit for the squared resolvent entries, time-averaged dynamical delocalization, and lower bounds on the localization length of most bulk eigenfunctions. Particularly, we allow the block size to be fixed or grow above a polylogarithmic threshold. In sufficiently large polynomial volumes, the dynamical estimates hold for \(C_\delta(\lambda+W/\lambda)\leq T\leq \lambda^{1+\kappa_d^{\rm BA}-\delta}\), with a dimension-dependent exponent \(\kappa_d^{\rm BA}>0\), and the spreading scale is \(\sqrt{(\lambda^3+\lambda W)T}\). This identifies a transition at \(W\asymp\lambda^2\) between \(\lambda^{3/2}\sqrt T\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda WT}\). The proof combines Gaussian moment estimates with deterministic stability of a matrix Dyson equation. A partial Bloch transform handles fixed blocks, while scalar reduction controls growing blocks. A Feshbach--Schur reduction of the block \(T\)-equation separates a single scalar diffusion mode from the stable internal cell modes. A renewal expansion and exact cell counting give a positive representation of the diffusion coefficient and control the fourth moment uniformly across the block-size transition. Notably, our argument does not require an enumeration of Feynman diagrams.
authors: Haoxuan Fu

papers.title: The exact information cost of randomized measurements in quantum metrology
papers.abstract: Randomized measurements provide state-independent readout for multiparameter quantum sensing. Although 3-designs retain a constant fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for every pure state, we show that 2-designs need not. In dimension \(d\), complete mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) retain exactly \(1/(d+1)\) of the QFI in the worst state and direction, attaining the universal lower bound for 2-designs built from orthonormal bases; symmetric informationally complete (SIC) measurements retain exactly \((1-1/\sqrt{d+1})/d\). The loss comes from aligned blind spots. Relative to a basis, pure-state changes split into population and phase parts of equal dimension, but probabilities respond only to the former.
