papers.title: Nonlinear Dynamics in Periodically Distributed Fibre Amplification Systems
papers.abstract: We investigate effects of longitudinally varying nonlinearity on periodically distributed amplification systems in optical fibres. Emphasis is made on configurations in which the nonlinear coefficient exponentially grows or decays along the propagation distance, while the group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) coefficient is held constant. Such systems are of practical relevance to the design of highly efficient nonlinear devices, including broadband light sources and advanced amplification schemes, where precise management of the interplay between the GVD, nonlinearity, and gain is essential. Adopting the known generic integrability condition, we derive exact analytical expressions for the evolution of the optical field in the presence of the tailored nonlinearity profiles and periodically distributed gain. The resulting periodic wavetrain solutions and their long-wave limit in the form of bright and dark solitons provide insight into the controlled enhancement or suppression of nonlinear effects under realistic amplification conditions. The robustness of these solutions is examined by introducing finite perturbations and directly evaluating their effects on the corresponding intensity profiles. The structural stability of solutions against deviations from the integrability condition is demonstrated too. Outcomes of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the nonlinear pulse dynamics in engineered gain-managed fibres and offer guidance for the development of novel optical systems, where the spatial distribution of the nonlinearity is exploited to optimise the performance.
authors: Sunday O. Atuba, Boris A. Malomed

papers.title: On Estimating Quantum Divergences with $p$-Power Means
papers.abstract: We study the problem of estimating the quantum divergence with $p$-power means, $\Phi_p(\rho\,\|\,\sigma)$. This quantity was investigated by Lam and Le (\textit{Linear Algebra Appl.}\ 2021). For any constant $p \in (0, 1)$, we present sample-efficient and query-efficient quantum algorithms for estimating $\Phi_p(\rho\,\|\,\sigma)$ and further show that estimating $\Phi_p(\rho\,\|\,\sigma)$ is $\mathsf{BQP}$-complete in the low-rank case.
authors: Jinge Bao, Minbo Gao, Qisheng Wang

papers.title: Benchmark Study for Quantum Statevector Simulators for Scientific Computing
papers.abstract: Quantum circuit simulators are essential for quantum algorithm development, yet systematic runtime benchmarks comparing major frameworks across CPU and GPU backends are limited. We benchmark three open-source frameworks - Cirq (qsim), CUDA-Q, and Qiskit (Aer) - on statevector simulation of the 2D quantum acoustic wave equation, evolved via Trotterized Hamiltonian dynamics, for problem sizes from 7 to 29 qubits on a single Azure virtual machine. The evaluation spans four categories: CPU runtime versus qubit count, strong scalability on multi-core CPUs at 27 qubits, GPU runtime versus qubit count, and GPU-over-CPU speedup. Relative rankings shift from one category to the next. On CPU, Cirq is fastest up to 23 qubits (2.4x faster than Qiskit at 21 qubits), but Qiskit overtakes it at larger sizes and higher thread counts, sustaining 80% parallel efficiency at 16 threads. On GPU, CUDA-Q leads between 13 and 21 qubits, while Cirq becomes the fastest GPU backend at large problem sizes, achieving 1.5x and 2.3x speedups over CUDA-Q and Qiskit at 29 qubits. GPU-over-CPU speedup ratios should be interpreted alongside absolute GPU runtimes; CUDA-Q's 1500x at 21 qubits is largely driven by the limited scaling of its CPU backend (qpp), and the absolute GPU runtimes show that the three frameworks' GPU backends differ by less than these ratios alone suggest. These results indicate that no single framework dominates across configurations, and that backend selection for statevector simulation should be guided by both target hardware and problem size.
authors: Timothy M. Yeo, Rodney W. Lessard

papers.title: All-to-All Connectivity in Superconducting Qubits via Metamaterial-Mediated Interactions
papers.abstract: We show that encoding superconducting qubits as dual-rail or spin-locked transmons lets a metamaterial waveguide couple them all-to-all while suppressing the spurious entanglement that burdens shared-mode architectures, a step toward the non-local connectivity that quantum low-density parity-check codes require. In a bare-transmon architecture, the dispersive coupling between each populated mode and every idle qubit attached to it entangles spectators with the gate, and cancelling it by dynamical decoupling lengthens every gate. The encoding suppresses this coupling at the hardware level, from second to fourth order in the inverse qubit--mode detuning. A two-tone cross-resonance drive then generates a M{\o}lmer-S{\o}rensen interaction between encoded qubits, which we use for an entangling gate and a joint parity measurement, both selective and parallelizable through different modes. Simulating two dual-rail transmons sharing three resonators with a mode lifetime of $30\,\mu$s, we find that heralding transmon relaxation as erasure leaves a gate infidelity of $1.4\times10^{-3}$ at $152$~ns, dominated by photon loss. Photon loss and mode crowding together bound the array size. The gate duration must exceed the inverse mode spacing, which shrinks as the array lengthens, while photon loss grows with gate duration. This bound grows linearly with the mode lifetime and with the inter-resonator coupling; at a lifetime of $150\,\mu$s, five times the simulated value, and a coupling of $80$~MHz, a $10^{-3}$ error budget admits $13$ qubits on $25$ resonators.
authors: Or Golan, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Andreas Butler, Gihwan Kim, Fernando G. S. L. Brand\~ao, Oskar Painter, Alex Retzker

papers.title: Daemon sub Ponte: The Cost of a Second Black Hole (A Scholium on an ER=EPR Thought Experiment)
papers.abstract: A thought experiment in the ER=EPR and related literature involves collecting the Hawking radiation of an old black hole, then collapsing it into a second, entangled black hole. In this short note, we examine the resources required by this idealized conversion. More specifically, we are interested in answering the question: how much external energy is needed to form the second black hole? Assuming a semiclassical bound on the information capacity of the newly formed black hole, we derive a conditional lower bound on external energy and a complementary constraint on correlations retained by the exterior degrees of freedom. We also distinguish entropy-level feasibility from the requirements for exact and approximate purification. We illustrate these requirements via a Page curve analysis.
authors: Yen Chin Ong

papers.title: Pump-scheme dependence of few-emitter lasers: exact multilevel correlations and photon statistics
papers.abstract: Few-emitter laser models usually replace the excitation cycle of the gain medium by a single Markovian pump jump of a two-level emitter. We test this replacement with the cavity and laser-transition parameters held fixed and the two-level pump rate fitted to the same mean photon number, using an exact damping-basis continued-fraction solution of the cavity--emitter master equation for $N$ identical $d$-level emitters with arbitrary independent incoherent transitions and one cavity-coupled transition, in the known reduced space of level populations and lasing coherences. First, a pump-quantum filtration shows that the inter-emitter coherence of $\Lambda$ and ladder media starts at second rather than first order in the pump; we evaluate its leading coefficient from the exact finite-system series and map the recycling rate at which its sign changes. Second, at matched photon number, rate-limited steps in the pump cycle push the long-time output-counting Fano factor of two and three emitters well below one: for two emitters it reaches 0.66 at a mean cavity occupation of 0.3 and is still 0.74 at an occupation of one, where $g^{(2)}(0)$ is within 3% of unity, because the anticorrelation sits at delays of about half a cavity lifetime rather than at zero delay. For two and three emitters the fitted two-level model gets both statistics wrong and places the output above the shot-noise level. Against independent single-emitter lasers at the same output, the common cavity erodes rather than enhances this single-emitter effect.
authors: Stephan Hartmann

papers.title: Density functionals for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We develop a density-functional theory for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian of nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics in the spirit of the convex-analytic formulation of Lieb. We consider finitely many electrons, subject to external scalar and vector potentials, coupled to the full continuum of massless transverse photons with an ultraviolet cutoff. The natural basic variables are the standard electron density and a combined current density, the sum of the paramagnetic current density and a field-induced current density generated by the quantized vector potential. We prove representability results for these density-current pairs and show that the mixed-state constrained-search functional attains its infimum and coincides with the Lieb functional obtained by convex conjugation. Since arbitrarily soft photons purify mixed states at a negligible energy cost without changing their density and combined current density, the pure-state Levy-Lieb functional equals the Lieb functional and is therefore convex, even though its infimum need not be attained. In addition, we establish the zero-coupling limit, which recovers the mixed-state Vignale-Rasolt functional of current-density-functional theory. Finally, we consider the long-wavelength (dipole) limit and show that the limiting functional can be written as a constrained search for the well-known length-gauge dipole Hamiltonian.
authors: Mih\'aly A. Csirik, Andre Laestadius, Markus Penz, Erik I. Tellgren

papers.title: Cooling-path-selected self-assembly of telecom InAsP quantum dots
papers.abstract: Epitaxial quantum dots are leading solid-state sources of quantum light, but reproducible growth on indium phosphide (InP) remains challenging because dot-formation windows are narrow and emission wavelengths are difficult to predict. Here we report a new epitaxial route for InAsP quantum dots on InP(001), in which the cooling path selects the final morphology without intentional deposition of group-III dot material. High-temperature As exposure forms a shallow near-surface InAsP layer through As-P exchange; the cooling path and continued As supply determine whether three-dimensional islands form. Surface-sensitive spectroscopy shows near-surface As enrichment, while cross-sectional STEM/EELS identifies graded, As-rich InAsP islands. The capped emitters span 1.2-1.6 micrometers, with single-photon emission observed up to 100 K. Across 20 wafers, the surface-effective exchange dose D provides a practical calibration for targeting the median emission wavelength. These results establish cooling as an active epitaxial step for telecom InAsP quantum-dot formation and wavelength control.
authors: Yiteng Zhang, Doaa Abdelbarey, Markus Etzkorn, Zenghui Jiang, Ankita Choudhary, Andreas Schaate, Tom Fandrich, Xin Cao, Chenxi Ma, Arijit Chakraborty, Eddy Patrick Rugeramigabo, Michael Zopf, Fei Ding

papers.title: Adiabatic pulsed-field dynamics of a frustrated spin-lattice system
papers.abstract: Magnetocaloric measurements in pulsed magnetic fields probe competing phases through the coupled evolution of magnetization and temperature. We formulate an adiabatic classical spin-lattice simulation that treats bond and site optical coordinates explicitly while representing the remaining thermal degrees of freedom by a finite internal reservoir. Magnetic work and energy exchange determine its temperature along each trajectory, providing feedback to the Langevin dynamics without external heat flow. Applied to a pyrochlore exchange-striction model motivated by CdCr$_2$O$_4$, the method produces a half-magnetization plateau, cooling near its onset, a temperature dome, and a change in cooling slope near plateau exit. Their joint emergence without an imposed temperature profile captures the experimental sequence of magnetic and thermal features. An approximate magnetization crossing near the temperature maximum is consistent with the reversible thermodynamic interpretation of the dome. The phenomenological reservoir enables this qualitative comparison within a simple model.
authors: Hidemaro Suwa

papers.title: Enriched Surface Thermodynamics for Sharp-Interface Fluid Models
papers.abstract: A sharp interface can retain material and structural information about an unresolved fluid transition zone. We formulate a local thermodynamic framework for isotropic surfaces carrying constituent surface mass densities and a thickness descriptor. The distinction between densities of additive contents and internal descriptors determines the area conjugate, reversible surface stress, and Gibbs-Duhem relation. A volume-per-area thickness has a pressure-like conjugate, a mechanical work contribution, and a separate evolution equation. Independent, constrained, and rapidly equilibrating thicknesses require different kinematics and reductions. Material storage can be retained without retaining surface inertia. The balances and entropy production specify admissible exchange and structural relaxation. For a moving surface patch, an available-free-energy identity accounts for mechanical power and for the contributions of material and structural fluxes across its boundary. Equilibrium reduction retains the production and transport needed to follow the reduced state. An explicit mass-thickness free energy has a positive-definite material Hessian and gives coupled adsorption, expansion, compression, and dissipative relaxation. Pressure response yields conditional restrictions on reduced states and demonstrates that distinct independent and constrained states can share an entire pressure-tension curve. Geometric thickness realizations and finite-rate transfer are treated with their associated mechanical and balance requirements. The framework separates state selection, constitutive closure, reduction, and identification from observations.
authors: Dieter Bothe

papers.title: Cuscuton Fifth Force: Implications of Non-Dynamical Scalars for Structure Growth
papers.abstract: The cuscuton is a scalar field that obeys a constraint rather than an evolution equation, so it modifies gravity without adding a propagating scalar degree of freedom. We study the cosmology of effective cuscuton theory when matter is minimally coupled in the Jordan frame, and therefore conformally coupled to the cuscuton in the Einstein-frame. We derive the background and linear perturbation equations and show that the algebraic cuscuton response mediates a fifth force even though the scalar itself does not propagate. The same conformal factor also changes Einstein-frame particle masses and the friction of matter perturbations, tying the strength and sign of the force to the background evolution rather than to an independent coupling. We study a power-law family of models which contain both tracking solutions and sign-switching solutions; in the latter the effective cuscuton density runs from negative during matter domination to a positive, cosmological-constant-like value today. Using a modified version of CLASS, including the induced particle-mass dependence of recombination, we illustrate the corresponding changes to CMB temperature and linear matter power spectra for benchmark models, without fitting to data. In the strongest benchmarks the fifth force changes the effective gravitational coupling on sub-horizon scales by about one percent, smaller than the accompanying changes to the matter power spectrum and the acoustic scale. For the sign-switching solutions this change is negative over most of cosmic history, so a non-propagating field can weaken rather than strengthen gravitational attraction.
authors: Adam Smith, Ilaria Andrei, Maria Mylova, Niayesh Afshordi

papers.title: Persistence of Fractal Structures in Iterated Quantum Protocols: Robustness to Preparation and Gate Errors
papers.abstract: Repeatedly combining entangling gates on an ensemble of qubits with measurement and postselection on a part of them induces a nonlinear evolution of the unmeasured qubits' state, whose fractal convergence boundaries make the outcome sensitive to the initial state. We study a family of iterated protocols in which $n$ identical qubits are coupled by CNOT gates, $n-1$ of them are postselected, and a parametrized single-qubit unitary acts on the survivor. For orders $n=2$ to $5$, we map the box-counting dimension of the pure-state Julia sets over the complex parameter plane and identify the symmetries that constrain it. Allowing mixed initial states, we find that moderate preparation noise preserves the main parameter-dependent trends of the boundary dimension over much of the studied range, and that the three-dimensional quasi-Julia boundary in the Bloch ball has a dimension that is approximately equal to the dimension of the pure-state Julia set plus one. We further model gate imperfections by an effective depolarizing channel and by fixed coherent interactions. Weak errors leave the estimated dimensions consistent with their ideal values even where the convergence regions visibly deform, and $ZZ$ errors are shown to be exactly conjugate to the ideal protocol at a rotated parameter. Finally, we analyze the postselection and storage cost of an implementation and propose a diagnostic test combining conditional fidelity with acceptance statistics, which we demonstrate on IQM Emerald and Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q.
authors: Attila Portik, Orsolya K\'alm\'an, Tam\'as Kiss

papers.title: Chaos, Fractals, and Ergodicity in Nonlinear Quantum Protocols
papers.abstract: Iterated nonlinear quantum protocols provide a straightforward way of realizing nonlinear dynamics in quantum systems through measurement and postselection. We investigate a family of protocols in which the order of the induced nonlinearity is controlled by the number of qubits involved in a single step. By examining the resulting rational maps and applying a set of numerical diagnostics, we identify extended parameter regions that exhibit ergodic-like dynamics for protocol orders $n=3,4,$ and $5$. We further characterize the associated chaotic behavior through the distribution of Lyapunov exponents. Our results show that ergodic-like dynamics persists beyond the quadratic case, while the geometry of the corresponding parameter regions and the typical degree of chaoticity depend strongly on the order of the nonlinear transformation.
authors: Attila Portik, Orsolya K\'alm\'an, Tam\'as Kiss

papers.title: Model-Based Fast Calibration for a Nitrogen Vacancy Center QPU
papers.abstract: We present a simulation-informed calibration workflow for NV quantum processing units that combines a digital twin, optimal control pulses, and a Fisher-information-guided experiment design into an iterative parameter estimation feedback loop. We find that using this framework, we obtain the same calibration precision as standard techniques with up to 4x reduction in measurement time.
authors: Tobias F. Sjolander, Marco Rossignolo, Lorena C. Bianchet, Swathi Hegde, Anurag Saha Roy, Thomas Lippert, Manpreet Singh Jattana

papers.title: From First Bond to Stable Adhesion: Multivalent Bond Stabilization in Receptor-Mediated Endocytosis
papers.abstract: After a particle forms its first receptor--ligand bond near a cell membrane, stable attachment often requires a threshold number of additional bonds. This paper develops a biophysical kinetic theory of this post-capture stage. The bond-number dynamics are modeled as a finite birth--death chain on $n=0,1,\dots,m$, where $0$ is loss of the initial bond and $m$ is the stabilization threshold. The mesoscopic rates $\lambda_n$ and $\mu_n$ encode the local energy landscape, accessible receptor--ligand pairs, steric and orientational constraints, and cooperative interactions within the growing cluster. The probability of reaching the threshold before losing the first bond is derived in closed form for general rates and, in the constant-ratio case, reduces to a geometric series controlled by the free-energy bias $\rho_n=\mu_n/\lambda_n$. The mean time to failure or stabilization follows from a tridiagonal backward equation. Conditioning on successful attachment is treated as a trajectory-selection effect: the conditioned chain is a Doob $h$-transform whose dissociation rate at $n=1$ vanishes, because successful trajectories cannot lose the first bond early. A minimal interface between the spatial first-capture probability and the bond-number chain is formulated, together with the conditions under which the stable capture probability factorizes into their product. The analysis shows that hitting probabilities constrain only the rate ratios, whereas the absolute rate scale requires time-resolved or dwell-time data. The threshold $m$ is a model-defined stabilization criterion, not a directly measured ligand count. The rates and threshold are effective parameters specified independently or inferred from kinetic data. The theory provides a quantitative framework for interpreting attachment probabilities, lifetimes, and the transition from first bond formation to stable multivalent adhesion.
authors: Hao Wu

papers.title: Exponential suppression of bit-flip errors in dissipative cat qubits
papers.abstract: We study the infinite-dimensional Lindblad generator $L_\epsilon=D[a^2-\alpha^2]+\epsilon D[a]$, describing a dissipative cat qubit subject to single-photon loss. For sufficiently large $\alpha$ and sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, we identify a two-dimensional spectral subspace near zero and establish an upper bound on the slow decay rate that decreases exponentially with $\alpha^2$, uniformly in $\epsilon$. This proves exponential suppression of bit-flip errors.
authors: Ruikang Liang, R\'emi Robin

papers.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schr\"odinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, where $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.
authors: Moises Gomez Solis

papers.title: Maximum purity of absolutely separable and absolutely PPT states in qutrit--qudit systems
papers.abstract: A bipartite state is absolutely positive partial transpose (APPT) if it remains PPT under every global unitary transformation, and absolutely separable if it remains separable. For every qutrit--qudit system $\mathbb{C}^3\otimes\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge3$, we prove that the maximum purity is the same for absolutely separable and APPT states and equals $\max\{(3n+8)/(3n+2)^2,\,3/(8n)\}$. The maximizing ordered spectrum is unique and contains exactly two distinct eigenvalues: the larger one has multiplicity one for $3\le n\le8$ and multiplicity $n$ for $n\ge9$. We also derive, in terms of the purity, an upper bound on the minimum partial-transpose eigenvalue achievable by global unitary transformations, and characterize all states for which the bound is attained. These results confirm the inscribed-polytope purity conjecture of Ahiable, Kothakonda, and Winter for all qutrit--qudit systems. They also give a lower bound, sharp over explicit purity ranges, on the global depolarizing noise needed for absolute separability or APPT.
authors: Anh T. Tran

papers.title: Heavy quark thermalization using phonon-heavy quark EFT
papers.abstract: The description of heavy quarks inside the QGP medium, especially at low momenta, remains challenging from first principles, due to large coupling strength and gluon occupation numbers. An alternative way to formulate a description in terms of perturbative degrees of freedom is the interaction of the heavy quarks with the collective excitations of the medium in the form of phonons. This description is derived as an effective field theory (EFT) and therefore allows for a natural occurring power counting of the allowed interactions. This EFT has already been established in our previous work, where we have derived the phonon-heavy quark interactions and calculated their thermal scattering cross section. In this work, we use these results, together with the heavy quark expansion, to calculate the heavy quark drag coefficient. Subsequently, we compare our results with the drag coefficient obtained from AdS/CFT calculations to determine the previously unknown Wilson coefficients for the quark-phonon coupling. Finally, we will use these coefficients to solve the Boltzmann equation for the heavy quark distribution, studying its thermalization in the QGP via soft phonon interactions.
authors: Andreas Kirchner, Berndt Mueller, Jyotirmoy Roy, Sebastian Waeber

papers.title: Hidden selection rules and amplitude ceilings in quantum Fourier models
papers.abstract: Quantum models with Pauli data encodings compute trigonometric polynomials whatever channels, ancillas and outcome-averaged measurements follow, so their expressivity depends on the Fourier coefficients a circuit can reach. We identify two kinds of structure that settle this before training. An antiunitary time-reversal rule and a unitary reflection rule remove frequencies. For gate-level circuits, deciding whether such a rule exists reduces to a linear system over GF(2), solvable in polynomial time, and the time-reversal rule holds in 17.6% of 6,120 configurations of standard templates. Single-upload encodings cap the top coefficient at $2^{-m}$ for every channel, and we compute the tight ceiling for every frequency and a depth-independent re-uploading bound. Frozen before training, these bounds were never violated on a non-linearity benchmark, and they predicted trained performance on real data. On IBM processors the rule held on a 65-qubit chain, and we switched rule-breaking relaxation noise on and off by design.
authors: Pavel Sulimov, Claude Lehmann

papers.title: Before the First Bond: Depletion-Assisted Stochastic Capture at the Onset of Endocytosis
papers.abstract: In a crowded extracellular environment, viruses and nanoparticles must reach the cell membrane within a few nanometers before the first ligand-receptor bond can form. Crowders generate an entropic depletion attraction, yet continuum models usually assume contact is already established or treat the approach deterministically. We formulate a thermodynamically consistent stochastic theory for this pre-contact stage. The sphere-plane depletion geometry uses the exact Asakur-Oosawa spherical-cap overlap, rather than a fitted cap, with either ideal van 't Hoff or pressure-only Carnahan-Starling osmotic pressure. A spatially varying near-wall mobility introduces a noise-induced drift that is essential for thermodynamic consistency and is often omitted. The first specific reaction is modeled by a Robin radiation boundary; the outer boundary is reflecting or absorbing. Three first-passage problems are solved analytically by quadrature: the mean reaction time, the reaction-before-escape probability, and the conditional success time, the last encoded by a Doob transform that exposes the selection bias of conditioning on capture. The theory separates thermodynamic inputs from conditional parameters and reveals a reaction-limited to diffusion-limited crossover controlled by the local Damk\"ohler number. For typical virus and nanoparticle parameters, the depletion well reaches $2$-$6\,k_{\rm B}T$, capture times are $0.1$-$1\,{\rm ms}$, and the conditional success time is measurably shorter than the unconditional mean. Finite-volume and Chebyshev schemes reproduce the analytic results within their discretization errors and satisfy the radiation-boundary mass balance. This provides a quantitative theoretical framework for crowding-assisted capture prior to membrane wrapping and a reference for comparing crowding, near-wall mobility, and surface reactivity in endocytosis.
authors: Hao Wu

papers.title: Floquet engineering of quantum relaxation
papers.abstract: Dynamical decoupling suppresses decoherence by averaging selected interactions between a quantum system and its environment. Here, we extend this notion through a general Floquet formalism that maps periodic control onto relaxation and dephasing channels. Environmental fluctuations are decomposed into Floquet components that sample the noise spectrum at distinct frequencies, with coupling strengths determined by control-induced Floquet coefficients. We experimentally investigate this approach using a single nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond under multi-pulse control. By tuning the drive and detuning, we reshape the coupling to environmental fluctuations and create isolated operating points where the dominant decoherence channel vanishes, strongly suppressing Floquet dephasing. The resulting coherence enhancement follows the predicted Floquet coupling coefficients and can be shifted by modifying the control sequence. These results establish Floquet driving as a general framework for engineering transverse and longitudinal relaxation through the design of quantum control protocols.
authors: Kang Xu, Dionisio Cendoya, Nazar Delegan, Daniela Pagliero, Lisandro Buljubasich, Carlos A. Meriles

papers.title: Theoretical estimation of nonlinear response function and ultrafast optical spectroscopy of nitrogen vacancy centers
papers.abstract: The theoretical description of the ultrafast optical response of nitrogen-vacancy centers has traditionally been developed using the nonlinear response function formalism based on a displaced harmonic oscillator model. However, restrictive defect geometries that lead to rich phonon mode distributions can limit the validity of this model. Here, we extend this framework by incorporating state-dependent oscillator modes characterized by different frequencies. We demonstrate that, as a consequence, the nonlinear response function is modified by a straightforward correction term that can be evaluated using operator algebraic techniques. These modifications directly impact two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy, which serves as a vital characterization tool for color centers by resolving ultrafast correlated electron-vibrational dynamics.
authors: Arunangshu Debnath

papers.title: Graph-Covariant Bottom-Up Scale-Bridging Reconstruction of Ground and Excited States of Extended Systems
papers.abstract: We propose a hierarchical scale-bridging construction for building first principles electronic structure models of extended molecular aggregates with disorder, and its practical realization in exciton systems. The general construction, referred here as to the encapsulation, is based on a recursive operator-valued hierarchy cast in a dual graph-theoretic (discrete) and configuration-space (continuous) structure, in which variables associated with a coarser level parameterize operators governing the degrees of freedom at the next finer level in a graph-covariant, geometry-preserving fashion. In an exemplary application of this scheme, aggregate-level ground- and excited-state operators are constructed through a many-body expansion (MBE), with matrix elements evaluated in a basis comprising the aggregate ground state and local Frenkel excitations. The required monomer and dimer building blocks are obtained from DFT and TDDFT calculations, yielding aggregate-level 1-particle transition density matrices as well as Hamiltonian, dipole moment and other operators that can be evaluated at the level of the building blocks. Starting from structural models obtained from experiment or molecular dynamics, this approach generates aggregate-level operators in a bottom-up fashion without fitting parameters to spectroscopic data or performing calculations on larger system cutouts. A numerical demonstration is given for an excitonic manifold in crystalline quaterthiophene. In particular, through its intrinsic configuration-dependence encoded in the encapsulations, it will provide a bridge between static electronic structure calculations for realistic, structurally disordered aggregates and quantum or quantum-classical simulations of exciton-vibrational dynamics.
authors: Bartosz B{\l}asiak, Irene Burghardt

papers.title: Logical-Class Diagnostic Layer for Stabilizer Codes and Decoders via Supercharge Structures
papers.abstract: We develop a decoder-agnostic logical-class diagnostic layer for abelian Pauli stabilizer codes, motivated by fault-tolerant quantum computing. An ancilla fermionic register defines a nilpotent supercharge whose clean degree-zero harmonic sector is the code space. Projected-return blocks derived from graded commutators organize the recovery test of whether a decoder-selected correction preserves every encoded input for every error in a declared same-syndrome family; the passing syndromes form the certified faithful window. Demoting the supercharge to an exact binary diagnostic formulation classifies residuals modulo stabilizers, separating a check violation, a harmless stabilizer residual, and a syndrome-silent nontrivial logical action, with a two-sector form for CSS codes. Because the unknown fault cancels, the relative logical class of two record-compatible candidates is computable online. We verify the diagnostic formalisms on the Steane code and specify a static--circuit bridge audit protocol for the Gross bivariate-bicycle quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code. The method supplements existing decoders without additional physical qubits for software use.
authors: Hai Lin

papers.title: A GPU-Accelerated and Geometry-Aware Quantum-Classical Framework for Optimized PES Scans with CUDA-Q
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical workloads, particularly Potential Energy Surface (PES) scans in quantum chemistry using batched VQE and QAOA, involve many structurally similar Hamiltonians differing only in coefficients. Existing warm-start and meta-optimization strategies reuse parameters between instances but still consume fixed quantum-classical resources, ignoring cross-instance structural similarities. We present OptiPESS, a GPU-accelerated runtime system for adaptive resource allocation in hybrid quantum-classical execution. OptiPESS introduces the Locality-Occupancy-Variance (LOV) metric, a lightweight, geometry-aware measure of Hamiltonian similarity, coupled with efficient alignment and Pauli-classification passes. Using LOV, OptiPESS performs distance-aware scheduling of iteration and shot budgets, predicting which instances can be skipped, quick-solved, or fully optimized. Implemented atop CUDA-Q with persistent multi-GPU execution and near-linear scaling, OptiPESS reduces classical and quantum evaluations by up to 78.3\% and wall-time by up to 74.8\% while maintaining baseline accuracy. This demonstrates how lightweight static analysis and adaptive scheduling can transform quantum-classical co-execution from fixed-budget loops into a predictive, resource-aware runtime.
authors: Panayiotis Christou, Shuwen Kan, Ying Mao

papers.title: Perfectness of partial Christoffel transforms of Nikishin systems
papers.abstract: We study multiple orthogonal polynomial systems obtained from a Nikishin system of two measures by applying a Christoffel transform to one of the measures at a point $x=x_0$. We show that if $x_0$ separates the supports of the generating measures, then the modified systems remain perfect. As an application, we prove that the type I multiple orthogonal polynomials of a Nikishin system have no zeros in the gap between the supports of its generating measures.
authors: Rostyslav Kozhan

papers.title: Beyond-RTA magnetoconductivity of multifold semimetals under generic orientations of electromagnetic fields
papers.abstract: We present an exact solution of the linearised semiclassical Boltzmann equation (SBE) beyond the relaxation-time approximation for multifold semimetals under arbitrarily oriented electric and magnetic fields. The framework treats the Berry curvature, orbital magnetic moment, Lorentz-force operator, and scattering terms on equal footing. Momentum-independent scattering-amplitudes couple the Fermi-surface sheets through intranode, interband, and internode processes. The scattering kernel has a finite rank and the SBE reduces to a linear system for a few moments, which is closed by the electron-number constraint. We apply this approach to four systems involving quadratic-corrected triple-point, Weyl, and Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl nodes, including tilted triple-point nodes. We obtain analytical results at zero field and to leading orders in the magnetic field, alongside numerical solutions for the full field dependence. Our results elucidate the roles of the topological properties, Lorentz-force operator, tilt, and intra- and internode scatterings in shaping the magnetoelectric conductivity. It cures severe shortcomings of previous treatments like incomplete ans\"atze and incomplete treatment of the Lorentz-force operator.
authors: Ipsita Mandal

papers.title: Plasmon modes in three-dimensional multifold semimetals. II. Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl and Kramers-Weyl nodes
papers.abstract: We investigate collective charge excitations in three-dimensional multifold semimetals in which multiple bands cross the Fermi level at a positive chemical potential, focusing on pseudospin-3/2 Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl semimetals and on Kramers-Weyl semimetals. Both systems host multiple concentric Fermi surfaces at positive chemical potential. Within the random-phase approximation, we analyse the density response, Drude weights, dielectric function, plasmon modes and their Landau damping, and Friedel oscillations, considering both small and arbitrary momentum transfers. In our companion work, arXiv:2610.18629, we investigated pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals, with and without a quadratic correction to their dispersion, as well as Hopf and Weyl semimetals. Comparing these systems allows us to elucidate the distinct roles of band dispersions and eigenstates in shaping collective charge dynamics. Our results demonstrate that collective charge excitations can distinguish multifold nodes with multiple Fermi surfaces and reveal information encoded in their eigenstates beyond that contained in the single-particle dispersion.
authors: Ipsita Mandal

papers.title: Boson sampling is fragile to loss
papers.abstract: Boson sampling experiments aim to demonstrate quantum computational advantage with increasing numbers of interfering photons. A central question is whether their computational hardness survives under photon loss. We show that even an arbitrarily small nonzero uniform loss rate permits efficient classical sampling in the average case when the rate remains fixed as the system grows. We exploit how loss suppresses correlations involving many photons to approximate the full output distribution using low correlation orders. The resulting samplers run in time polynomial in system size and inverse total variation error, with the error averaged over Haar random interferometers. The results apply to Fock state boson sampling with single-photon states in distinct input modes and arbitrary additional vacuum inputs, and to Gaussian boson sampling with equal squeezing of bounded strength in every input mode. Classical sampling is efficient even when the mean detected photon number grows linearly with system size, showing that large photon counts alone do not ensure computational hardness.
authors: Youngrong Lim

papers.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: KPZ universality
papers.abstract: We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and positive representing measure, together with joint profile convergence at every prescribed finite parameter list. We also prove convergence of the height evolution from general upper-semicontinuous initial profiles to the half-space KPZ fixed point. The associated passage field converges locally uniformly to the half-space directed landscape, jointly with evolutions from finitely many initial profiles driven by the same environment. The convergence results cover the critical boundary window and every fixed subcritical boundary rate, including zero. All fixed subcritical rates produce the same limiting laws.
authors: Kailun Chen

papers.title: No infinite cluster at criticality for long-range percolation with fast-decaying interactions
papers.abstract: We consider independent long-range bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in which $x$ and $y$ are joined with probability $1-e^{-\beta J(x-y)}$. Let $d\ge2$ and let $J$ be invariant under coordinate permutations and sign changes, positive on nearest-neighbour pairs, and satisfy $\liminf_{n\to\infty} n^d\sum_{\|x\|>n}J(x)=0$. We prove that there is no infinite cluster at the critical parameter. Together with Berger's theorem for heavy tails, this gives continuity of the phase transition for $J(x)\asymp\|x\|^{-d-\alpha}$ for every $\alpha>0$ except $\alpha=d$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for every exponentially decaying kernel satisfying these hypotheses. Previously the fast-decaying case was known for nearest-neighbour and uniform finite-range kernels, in $d=2$ for finite-range and exponential kernels, and in high dimension for sufficiently spread-out kernels. The proof adapts a recent renormalization argument for nearest-neighbour percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ that is driven by a gluing inequality conjectured by Kozma and Nitzan. Long edges enter in two places: they can jump over the surfaces that a nearest-neighbour path must cross, and they let a cluster outside a box enter it from far away. We control the first with thick outer faces and the tail condition, and the second by measuring entrances through the total edge weight between a cluster and a box rather than through the number of boundary vertices.
authors: Yan Ru Pei

papers.title: Purity maxima, absolute separability, and spectral volumes of absolutely PPT states
papers.abstract: For $m\otimes n$ systems with $n\ge m\ge3$, we determine the exact maximum purity of absolutely positive partial transpose (APPT) states and the unique maximizing ordered spectrum when $n\ge2m^2-4$ for even $m$ or $n\ge2m^2-m-4$ for odd $m$. Under these dimension assumptions, absolutely separable states have the same maximum purity, attained at the same unique ordered spectrum. The proof uses an outer polytope defined by two linear head--tail inequalities, each comparing a sum of the largest eigenvalues with a sum of the smallest. Under explicit multiplicity assumptions, we derive an exact matrix criterion for APPT membership of full-rank spectra with three distinct eigenvalues. For every $m\ge10$, this criterion gives explicit APPT boundary spectra at $n=4m-2$ and $n=4m$ that disprove both cases of the maximum purity conjecture of Ahiable, Kothakonda, and Winter. We also determine the exact completely absolutely separable (CAS) purity maximum and its unique maximizing ordered spectrum in every bipartite dimension. We prove that the inner APPT polytope consists entirely of absolutely separable spectra. The resulting linear sufficient condition for absolute separability strictly improves the reduction-map and eigenvalue-ratio tests. Finally, we compute the exact relative volumes of the CAS set and an outer polytope defined by a single head--tail inequality. Under the uniform measure on spectra, the CAS, absolutely separable, and APPT volumes have the same asymptotic order $\sqrt n\,e^{-\kappa_m n}$ for every fixed $m\ge2$, with explicit $\kappa_m>0$.
authors: Anh T. Tran

papers.title: Eynard-Orantin Topological Recursions for Higher Weil-Petersson Volumes on Moduli Spaces of Super Riemann Surfaces
papers.abstract: We derive an Eynard-Orantin topological recursion for intersection numbers involving Norbury's $\Theta$-class together with $\psi$-classes and higher $\kappa$-classes. These intersection numbers encode higher Weil-Petersson volumes of moduli spaces of super Riemann surfaces. The resulting recursion is a higher-$\kappa$ deformation of the topological recursion associated with the Bessel curve, which encodes the Br\'ezin-Gross-Witten model.
authors: Dingkang Xiong, Jian Zhou

papers.title: On Emergent Geometry of the Generalized BGW Theory
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of the mathematical theory of the generalized Br\'ezin-Gross-Witten (BGW) theory using methods from statistical physics. We prove the multidifferentials of the generalized BGW theory are given by the Eynard-Orantin topological recursion in a generic background with general coupling constants. Furthermore, we characterize the transition between the Witten-Kontsevich model and the generalized BGW theory. This approach yields a new proof of the Okuyama-Sakai conjecture, further elucidating the deep structural connections between these two fundamental models.
authors: Dingkang Xiong, Jian Zhou

papers.title: Superradiance fingerprints of moir\'e exciton-biexciton condensates: path-entangled biphoton vs. supercurrent-enabled one-photon channel
papers.abstract: Hybrid moir\'e excitons form a dense array of electrically tunable single-photon emitters, entailing cooperative optical responses with intriguing consequences. With the strong dipole-dipole interaction, they also realize Bose-Hubbard quantum simulators of emergent correlated matter such as Bose-Einstein condensates (BEC). Here we reveal the characteristic cooperative radiation from condensates of hybrid moir\'e excitons in twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayers. In each individual moir\'e trap, the layer hybridization selection rule dictates that the ground-state exciton is a quantum emitter of orbital-angular-momentum photons, with an exceptionally long radiative lifetime. Ground-state emission becomes pronounced only upon forming condensates, where inter-sublattice dipole attraction and intra-sublattice repulsion together lead to the coexistence of exciton and biexciton BEC with comparable weights. The biexciton (molecular-type) BEC decays through superradiance of path-entangled biphotons, whereas the exciton (atomic-type) BEC is dark at rest and becomes superradiant when it carries a supercurrent. Our findings not only uncover a novel source of entangled light but also establish unique fingerprints for exploring the cold chemistry of atomic-molecular condensates with moir\'e excitons.
authors: Haochen Wang, Shengxian Li, Hongyu Lu, Mingxing Chen, Wang Yao

papers.title: Near-Optimal Learning of Quantum Many-Body Systems from Gibbs and Thermal Metastable States via the Stationarity Test
papers.abstract: We study the problem of learning a finite-range quantum Hamiltonian on an $n$-qubit $D$-dimensional lattice from copies of its Gibbs states at a known inverse temperature $\beta$ or its thermal metastable states. Existing efficient algorithms at arbitrary temperature have sample guarantees with an $e^{\poly(\beta)}$ dependence, leaving open whether the exponent can be made linear in $\beta$. We achieve this improvement: for $\beta\ge1$, our algorithm learns all Hamiltonian coefficients to $\ell_\infty$-error $\epsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ using $\tO\bigl(e^{O(\beta)}\epsilon^{-2}\log(n/\delta)\bigr)$ copies and total time $\tO\bigl(n e^{O(\beta)}\epsilon^{-2}\log(n/\delta)\bigr)$. The measurements act on individual copies and are supported on balls of radius $O\bigl(\beta^2+\beta\log(1/\epsilon)\bigr)$. Our sample complexity achieves the optimal exponential order in $\beta$, with optimal $\epsilon^{-2}$ dependence up to logarithmic factors. Building on the stationarity-test framework \citep{Bergamaschi2026Stationarity}, we prove a unified Fisher-information coercivity bound showing that errors in the candidate Hamiltonian produce a detectable signal with only an $e^{-O(\beta)}$ loss in sensitivity. The key is a smooth frequency filter whose bandwidth remains independent of temperature, together with sharper estimates relating this signal to the Hamiltonian coefficients. For thermal metastable states, the guarantee holds under local drift $\zeta\le e^{-C\beta^{2D+1}}$, for a geometry-dependent constant $C>0$, and above an accuracy floor $\tO(e^{O(\beta)}\zeta)$. The argument applies to both Gibbs and thermal metastable states and, combined with local measurements and projected stochastic gradient descent (SGD), yields both learning guarantees.
authors: Tai Hsuan Yang

papers.title: From Ghost SICs to SIC-POVMs: A Galois Reduction of Zauner's Conjecture
papers.abstract: Symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (SIC-POVMs, or SICs) are optimal minimal measurements for quantum state tomography. Problem~1 of Horodecki, Rudnicki and \.Zyczkowski's open problems in quantum information asks for SICs in infinitely many dimensions. By work of Appleby--Flammia--Kopp and Radchenko--Wheeler, ghost SICs, which satisfy the SIC equations with Hermiticity up to parity, exist unconditionally for $d\ge4$. We study the passage from ghosts to SICs. We compute all isolated points of the complexified SIC variety for $d=4,5,6$; exactly half are SICs. We prove that no symmetry of the SIC equations maps a ghost to a SIC, so the step is purely arithmetic, and that a SIC exists in dimension $d$ whenever the ghost overlap units satisfy a place law: each Galois conjugate is real or unimodular according to the infinite place of the real quadratic field $F$ below it. If the unit field is abelian over $F$, the place law is the Stark relation $c_-=\kappa$; equivalently, a Galois conjugate of an associated near-group fusion category is unitary exactly when it is pseudo-unitary. For $d$ a power of a prime $p\equiv5\pmod 6$ or of $3$, an infinite family, we prove that under the algebraic part of Stark's conjecture $c_-=\kappa$ is equivalent to the triviality of $\kappa$ on the Hilbert-class-field part of the unit field. That condition involves no complex conjugation, and it follows from a sign-free multiplet hypothesis. We state an explicit $GL_2$ reciprocity law for the squared ghost overlaps that implies $c_-=\kappa$, and we prove it for the computed algebraic overlaps in $d=5,7,11,15$ by Artin reciprocity and a check in every ray class. Zauner's conjecture remains open: the algebraic part of Stark's conjecture and the multiplet hypothesis are not proved here.
authors: Hassan Khodaiemehr

papers.title: The massive phase of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model is stable under small anisotropy
papers.abstract: Polyakov predicted that the classical Heisenberg model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature, and a proof of this has recently been posted. We show that the massive phase survives small anisotropy. For every inverse temperature $\beta$ there is $\delta(\beta)>0$ such that the $S^2$-valued model with couplings $\sum_iJ^i\sigma_x^i\sigma_y^i$ has exponentially decaying spin two-point functions, uniformly in finite subgraphs with free boundary conditions and in edge strengths up to $\beta$, whenever $|J^i-1|\le\delta(\beta)$ for $i=1,2,3$. For the easy-plane model with couplings $\sigma^x\sigma^x+\sigma^y\sigma^y+\lambda\sigma^z\sigma^z$ this shows that the onset of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, proved by Garban and de Montgolfier for every $\lambda\in(-1,1)$, moves to zero temperature as $\lambda\uparrow1$: in free-boundary limits, correlations decay exponentially for every $\beta\le c |\log(1-\lambda)|^{1/2}$. The physical prediction is of order $|\log(1-\lambda)|$. The same holds for aligned single-ion anisotropy, which includes a confining potential $\varepsilon\sum(\sigma^z)^2$, and for nearly isotropic $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$. The proof keeps the sign-cluster argument of the isotropic proof, using Ginibre's correlation inequality for anisotropic planar energies, and uses the rotation symmetry only on one finite annulus, where the anisotropy is a bounded perturbation of the Hamiltonian.
authors: Yan Ru Pei

papers.title: Access Resources and Stability of Error-Correction Capabilities in Continuous Strategic Codes
papers.abstract: Continuous quantum error correction depends on which parts of a measurement record remain available to the controller at recovery. We study this temporal access using continuous strategic codes, formulated as open continuous process tensors contracted with causal instruments and conditional recovery. For monitored stabilizer codes, a common-optimal-correction criterion identifies when records can be merged without loss and yields a factorization for separated CSS inference. Terminal decision labels and causal persistent memory carry different costs: five persistent classical states reach the complete-record optimum in a finite-strength counting model, whereas its two-window diffusive counterpart has nine terminal decision labels and requires unbounded memory for exact causal recovery. Uniform lower and constructive upper bounds establish an optimal fidelity deficit of order $m^{-2}$ for $m$ persistent states in the diffusive model. Counting and diffusive stability bounds translate open-process approximation into guarantees for deployed-controller performance and retained access advantages, quantified by explicit quantizers and model-mismatch curves. The same process--instrument framework connects storage with persistent environments and irreversible noise to spacetime interrogation and record-selected paths for a logical $T$ gate. These results specify which record distinctions recovery needs, the memory cost of approximating them, and the logical protection retained under model error.
authors: He Wang

papers.title: Haagerup vertex operator algebras at central charge eight
papers.abstract: Evans and Gannon showed that a positive vertex operator algebra of central charge eight whose representation category is the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category has one of two character vectors, with six or nineteen currents. Call such an algebra, if strongly rational, a Haagerup algebra. We prove that a Haagerup algebra $U$ has six currents, that $U_1 \cong \mathfrak{sl}_2 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2$ embeds into $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ in one of two explicit ways, with levels $(1,39)$ or $(3,13)$, and we determine the lowest weight spaces of its modules and $U_2$ as $U_1$-modules. For the levels $(3,13)$, $U_2$ is one of four Galois conjugate subspaces, and the algebra it generates is unitary, $C_2$-cofinite and isomorphic to the algebra constructed by Jiao; for the levels $(1,39)$, $U$ contains the algebra announced by Riesen. The associated lattice of $U$ is that of the form $x^2+xy+10y^2$, resp. $3x^2+3xy+4y^2$, the two classes of the principal genus of discriminant $-39$. Exchanging them in the decomposition of $U$ over its Heisenberg commutant gives a Haagerup algebra $U^\natural$ of the other levels, and $U \mapsto U^\natural$ is a bijection between the isomorphism classes of the two cases. Consequently, if either explicit algebra of Jiao or Riesen is positive and strongly rational with representation category braided equivalent to $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$, there are exactly two Haagerup algebras up to isomorphism, forming a single hyperbolic genus. The explicit algebras of Jiao and Riesen have rational forms. The proofs combine exact trace relations given by vector-valued modular forms, exact computations in a model of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$, and genera of vertex operator algebras.
authors: C\'edric Arhancet

papers.title: A Clifford-index approach connecting boundary Dirac fermions to sigma-model topological terms in the periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors
papers.abstract: The periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors emerges from two distinct approaches: boundary Anderson localization and momentum-space K-theory. Connecting these approaches physically requires deriving the boundary sigma-model topological terms from the underlying fermion theories. We develop an index-theoretic framework for minimal massless boundary Dirac models in the eight real Altland--Zirnbauer classes. Its central ingredients are an elliptic cylinder operator interpolating between two sigma-field textures, a quotient index defined by the cylinder's graded Clifford symmetry algebra, and an index theorem identifying its protected zero-mode index with the relative homotopy class of the endpoint textures. To establish this correspondence, we deform the cylinder texture while preserving the kernel's index class and localize the obstruction to a Clifford defect. An exact oscillator-kernel calculation fixes the generator normalization. A field-independent congruence and a common regularization provide a real antisymmetric Pfaffian representative whose sign transport is related to the cylinder mod-two index by Witten's spectral-flow argument. This yields the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_2$ theta weight for one minimal physical module. Combining complex-parent anomalies with physical Clifford multiplicities and real-target periods also gives the real-class Wess--Zumino terms with unit spherical level. The framework thus provides an operator-level connection between boundary Dirac theories and the sigma-model topological terms associated with the periodic table.
authors: Y. X. Zhao

papers.title: A Planar Switching Neuron Shares Logarithmic First-Spike Latency with Its Three-Dimensional Parent But Not Its Onset Mechanism
papers.abstract: Can a reduced neuron model reproduce first-spike latency scaling while changing how a stimulus initiates sustained firing? We compare a piecewise-linear planar Neurosimilator with its three-dimensional parent. Both exhibit logarithmic latency dependence over the investigated input intervals, with different fitted coefficients. The mechanisms differ. In the parent, sustained spiking and a stable resting focus coexist in a spiking--rest bistability regime. An abrupt step accesses spiking, while slow stimulation can retain rest at the same final input. Its step-induced firing threshold is therefore an operational basin-access threshold below the saddle-node limit point, not a loss of equilibrium stability. In the planar model, the resting equilibrium instead reaches a switching boundary while its subthreshold eigenvalues remain negative. We derive the planar latency law from this boundary approach. The model generates repetitive excursions without an imposed reset and admits exact trajectories within six switching regions. Similar measured latency scaling thus coexists with different mechanisms of access to firing. Validating a reduced model's mechanism of excitability requires examination of stimulus protocol and attractor access alongside equilibrium structure and spike timing.
authors: Giorgio Sonnino, Vadim Shlyonskiy, Thomas Erneux, David Gall

papers.title: Precision determination of $B_c$ and $B_c^*$ meson decay constants from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We present a lattice QCD study of heavy-heavy meson decay constants using the HISQ gauge ensemble generated by the MILC Collaboration. Employing the HISQ action for both charm and bottom valence quarks tuned to their physical masses, we determine pseudoscalar, vector, and tensor decay constants for heavy quarkonium and $B_c$ systems. Preliminary results are presented for the decay constants of the $B_c$, $B_c^*$, $\eta_c$, $\eta_b$, and $\Upsilon$ mesons.
authors: Navdeep Singh Dhindsa, Debsubhra Chakraborty, Nilmani Mathur

papers.title: Chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in flavor branes
papers.abstract: We investigate the chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in the chiral symmetry broken phase of the holographic D3/D7 model with massless quarks, where the axial charge in the flavor sector can relax through transfer to the adjoint sector in the probe limit. We find that the dispersion relations of the quasi-normal modes are well described by the phenomenological expression for the chiral magnetic wave when the relaxation rate is small. We then determine how this rate depends on vector charge density and the chiral condensate. At higher temperatures, it increases with charge density and decreases with increasing condensate, while these dependences become non-monotonic at lower temperatures. These results show that the phenomenological description of the chiral magnetic wave also applies in the chiral symmetry broken phase in the quasi-hydrodynamic regime.
authors: Masataka Matsumoto, Kensei Tanaka

papers.title: Bounds and sufficient conditions in quantum Zeno effect
papers.abstract: When a quantum system undergoes a series of repeated measurements during its time evolution to check whether it remains in the initial state, the resulting state lifetime can decrease (the quantum Zeno effect) or increase (the quantum inverse Zeno effect) as the inter-measurement period increases. Several transitions between these two regimes may occur within the same system. A carefully chosen measurement period $\tau_\ast$ (or rate $r_\ast$ in the case of a stochastic measurement protocol) brings the state lifetime to its global minimum. Here, we describe the upper and lower bounds on the optimized state lifetime, which are expressed in terms of characteristic time scales encoded in the state survival probability $P(T)$, which is assumed to decrease monotonically to zero at large $T$. In addition, we analyze the bounds on the optimal measurement periods/rates and formulate sufficient conditions for observing the inverse Zeno effect. The analysis is also extended to states with non-monotonic survival functions. The results are illustrated numerically with an example of a system of optically trapped ultra-cold atoms.
authors: Vladimir Parfenyev, Sergey Belan

papers.title: Decoherence suppression in quantum dense coding
papers.abstract: By harnessing entanglement to transmit information beyond the limits of classical communication, quantum dense coding serves as a key component in various quantum technologies. However, in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum era, noise-induced decoherence poses inevitable challenges to its practical implementation. By investigating the non-Markovian decoherence dynamics of the two categories of quantum dense coding protocols realized in discrete- and continuous-variable systems, we demonstrate a physical mechanism to suppress the decoherence in quantum dense coding. It is found that the formation of a bound state in the energy spectrum of the entire system consisting of each subsystem and its local environment of the quantum channel restores the quantum advantage of dense coding in the presence of decoherence. Refreshing our understanding on the noisy effect on quantum dense coding, our finding offers a guide toward the practical realization of noise-tolerant quantum dense coding.
authors: Xi Yan, Wen-Jie Zhang, Jun-Hong An

papers.title: Optimal Control of Chemical Reaction Networks with Thermodynamic Cost
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic control seeks to realize desired functions at minimal thermodynamic cost, yet existing frameworks remain largely confined to slow driving regimes or state-to-state transport. Here we establish a thermodynamic optimal-control theory for Markov jump processes (MJPs) and chemical reaction networks (CRNs) that accommodates objectives over both states and reaction fluxes beyond slow-driving limit. By deriving the thermodynamic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation, we demonstrate that the optimal dynamics take the form of a perturbed generalized-gradient flow driven by the value function. A convex representation of the entropy-production rate via generalized means identifies its Legendre--Fenchel dual as the dissipation function. The resulting dynamics shares the thermodynamic structure of CRNs and admits an information-geometric characterization. We further derive a thermodynamic Pontryagin equation by recasting the control problem in terms of thermodynamic forces, providing a complementary description of optimal trajectories and clarifying connections to thermodynamic optimal transport. Our results establish a thermodynamic and geometric foundation for controlling MJPs and CRNs beyond mere transport, opening avenues for optimizing biological processes and finite-time thermodynamic operations in far-from-equilibrium regimes.
authors: Tetsuya J. Kobayashi, Alix Robin, Shuhei A. Horiguchi

papers.title: Mitigating sloppiness with intermediate controls in sequential multiparameter spin interferometry
papers.abstract: Multiparameter quantum sensing requires different parameters to produce distinguishable probe responses while allowing their information to be extracted simultaneously. In sequential sensing without intermediate control, two phases encoded through the same generator are locally indistinguishable. Here we show that parameter-independent intermediate controls overcome this limitation in a collective-spin interferometer by separating the corresponding effective generators in the probe covariance geometry. Specifically, a transverse collective rotation provides an analytically tractable realization, and intermediate one-axis twisting (OAT) generates additional nonlinear operator directions and a broad regime of enhanced joint estimation. For fixed total particle number $N$ and matched twisting resource, both marginal precision bounds lie below those of a separated-OAT strategy while measurement incompatibility remains weak. For intermediate OAT, conditional optimization of an upper bound on the Holevo cost yields asymptotic $N^{-2}$ scaling. For this protocol, a fixed rotated-Dicke measurement retains simultaneous two-parameter enhancement over a broad phase region. These results show that nonlinear intermediate control can mitigate sloppiness while preserving quantum-enhanced precision with a common readout.
authors: Hai Feng, Xinwei Li, Rong Lu, Li You

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced multiphase estimation with spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced two-phase estimation in a spin-$1$ Bose-Einstein condensate, where spin-exchange collisions generate a spin-nematic squeezed state in the $m_F=\pm1$ modes. The resulting pair-correlated state has a rank-one quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) for the two mode phases relative to the $m_F=0$ mode and therefore cannot resolve them independently. Nevertheless, we find that a parameter-independent passive three-mode transformation lifts this rank deficiency and enables joint estimation of both phases. In the undepleted-pump regime, we derive expressions for the QFIM, optimize the equal-weight multiparameter quantum Cram\'er-Rao bound, and obtain a full-rank probe with squeezing-enhanced sensitivity below the matched fixed-total-number standard quantum limit (SQL). These analytical predictions are confirmed by exact-diagonalization calculations. We further construct a parameter-independent readout that maps the phase combinations onto displacement channels accessible through atomic homodyne or parity measurements. Our results provide a route from spin-mixing-generated quantum correlations to two-phase estimation in spinor condensates.
authors: Jiaheng Jin, Xinwei Li, Dong E. Liu, Li You

papers.title: An Observable-Algebra Approach to Quantum Coherence in Anyonic Systems
papers.abstract: Physical restrictions on operations can make quantum coherence inaccessible. Quantifying off-diagonal density matrix elements in a chosen basis alone does not reveal which information is hidden by each restriction. To distinguish their effects, we describe physical restrictions through subalgebras of accessible observables. The associated trace-preserving conditional expectations unify two reconstruction principles: each gives both the maximum-entropy state compatible with the accessible data and the closest state in the corresponding subalgebra in relative entropy. We apply this framework to anyonic systems to separate the contributions from local-charge superselection and non-Abelian fusion rules. We prove that the charge-line severing map is the conditional expectation onto the local-product subalgebra. It is completely positive and quantum-trace-preserving, and uniquely reconstructs a state in this space from all local-product expectation values. The hierarchy of measurement restrictions then separates total bipartite coherence into three nonnegative contributions: coherence between local charges, inaccessible fusion information, and conventional coherence. The first two decompose the anyonic charge entanglement and distinguish the effects of local-charge superselection from the remaining fusion information. Finally, we relate basis-independent measures of anyonic coherence to entanglement. For pure anyonic states with vacuum total charge, the optimized total and correlated coherence equal the total and conventional relative-entropy entanglement, respectively.
authors: Cheng-Qian Xu, D. L. Zhou

papers.title: Stochastic Orders of the Exit Pair and the Monotone Response to Resetting
papers.abstract: Resetting a process, that is, restarting it from its initial position at random times, changes the probability that it leaves an interval through one end rather than the other. We show that the direction of this change is governed by how the exit time depends on the exit side, and we express this through classical stochastic orders. For random walks and birth-death chains we determine when resetting more intensively always moves the exit probability in the same direction, and we show that this can fail: we give an explicit chain in which the direction reverses twice over time, and bound the number of such reversals spectrally. We also show how the direction depends on the starting point. In the continuum limit we obtain the corresponding results for diffusions with drift.
authors: Tony Newton, Juan Antonio Vega Coso

papers.title: Quantum Lower Bounds for Collision Problems
papers.abstract: We establish tight lower bounds on the adaptive and non-adaptive quantum query complexities of Promised $k$-to-one Finding on an exactly $k$-to-one input string $x\in\mathbb Z_q^n$, for every fixed $k\ge2$ and every feasible alphabet size $q\ge n/k$. The lower bounds are $\Omega_k(n^{1/2-1/(2(2^k-1))})$ for unrestricted adaptive algorithms and $\Omega_k(n^{1-1/k})$ for one-round non-adaptive algorithms. The former matches the adaptive quantum algorithm of Liu and Zhandry [LZ19], whereas the latter matches classical birthday sampling even when the parallel queries are arbitrarily entangled. We also establish the non-adaptive lower bound $\Omega_k(\sqrt{n/k})$ for $k$-to-one Testing when $q\ge n$, resolving an open question posed by Koiran, Landes, Portier, and Yao [KLPY10]. Our proofs generate the balanced input from a uniformly random permutation and use compressed permutation oracles to describe the information learned by the algorithm. The adaptive proof bounds the growth of partial collisions through successive queries. The one-round proof instead analyzes the state after the parallel queries directly, bounding the probability that the compressed database contains a full collision. In both proofs, a short verification step accounts for correct outputs that include unrecorded positions. For the decision problem, we also compare one-round states with independent and distinct output labels.
authors: Pan Peng, Jingyu Wu

papers.title: Heavy-meson molecules with dynamical pions
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy-meson molecules by treating the pion as a dynamical degree of freedom. We construct an energy-independent Hamiltonian that couples the two- and three-body Fock spaces. The two-body sector contains a pseudoscalar meson and a vector meson $H_1H_2^{*}$, while the three-body sector consists of two pseudoscalar mesons and a pion $H_1H_2 \pi$. The $H^*$ self-energy, the $H_1H_2^{*}$ pion-exchange interaction, and the $H_1H_2\pi$ three-body propagation are consistently generated through the coupling between the two Fock sectors. We use the Gaussian expansion and complex scaling methods to solve the coupled Schr\"odinger equation. Previous approaches usually reduce three-body effects to energy-dependent two-body kernels and solve the equations iteratively. Our approach obtains the poles by solving a single linear generalized eigenvalue problem. The eigenvectors also provide explicit wave functions in both Fock sectors, allowing a qualitative analysis of channel weights and spatial structure. We benchmark the framework in $T_{cc}^{+}$ and $X(3872)$. The benchmark results are consistent with the current experimental pole determinations. We then apply this formalism to the $BB\pi$, $B\bar{B}\pi$, $DB\pi$ and $D\bar{B}\pi$ systems. We predict one isoscalar bound state in each of these systems. The $DB\pi$ and $D\bar{B}\pi$ systems also contain resonances lying below and above their three-body threshold, respectively. We propose complementary searches for these resonances through $DB^*\to DB\gamma$ and $D\bar B\pi$. This coupled Fock-space framework can be readily extended to other few-body systems in which unstable constituents can decay and change the particle number.
authors: Yan-Ke Chen, Liang-Zhen Wen, Lu Meng, Shi-Lin Zhu

papers.title: Three New Phases in the Two-Dimensional Potts Model at Complex Temperature
papers.abstract: The complex-temperature phase structure of the two-dimensional Potts model has remained largely unresolved despite decades of study. Here we determine the complex-temperature phase diagram of the 3-state Potts model, and uncover three gapless phases beyond the familiar ferromagnetic and paramagnetic phases. This is done by combining tensor-network free energies with the Poisson equation to compute the Fisher zero density in the thermodynamic limit. The resulting zero distribution unifies and revises long-standing conjectures on the zero loci, and outlines each phase. One is a non-conformal gapless phase, with an exponentially growing number of low-lying transfer-matrix levels distributed across all momentum sectors. The other two are Luttinger-liquid phases with complex-valued Luttinger parameters related by the Kramers-Wannier duality. At the antiferromagnetic critical point, the Luttinger parameter equals 3, while its limit from the adjacent Luttinger-liquid phase is 6. These findings reveal rich phase structures and unconventional critical behavior in a classical textbook model.
authors: Fang-Cheng Wang, Qi-Jun Ye, Xin-Zheng Li

papers.title: Quantum Recovery from Black-Hole Radiation Beyond the Emission Yield
papers.abstract: A proposed resolution of the black-hole information paradox must explain which information an outside observer can recover from escaping radiation\cite{Hawking,Page,Hayden,Almheiri}. Environmental memory can return correlations to the source without delivering them to that observer\cite{ChenQi,ChenMemory}. Here we establish a sharp recovery frontier at fixed mean radiation yield for single-excitation channels and realize its qubit limit with an autonomous quantum-memory emitter. Unequal transmissions balance retained coherence against information in failed collection events. A reference--radiation correlation test distinguishes this gain even when the mean collected energy is unchanged. Identical transmission channels instead give the same recovery at matched collection, regardless of their emission timescales. For a broader class of interacting sources, an ordering of collected and inaccessible coupling spectra forbids unassisted quantum transmission irrespective of internal memory. A separate coding example supports a positive rate where uniform transmission at matched actual yield has zero capacity. Together, these results identify what openness must change to assist recovery: the accessible transmission structure. They supply a physically constrained comparison of evaporation mechanisms, separating information delivered to radiation from coherence retained elsewhere or an increase in the collected output.
authors: Kashif Ammar Yasir

papers.title: A General Manifestly Covariant Construction of Partial-Wave Amplitudes in the Rarita-Schwinger Formalism
papers.abstract: We propose a new set of functions, named Relative Spin Wave Functions (RSWFs), defined via covariant pure boosts to a common rest frame. RSWFs separate spin transport from orbital-spin coupling while preserving the conventional partial-wave angular structure in a manifestly covariant form. Within the Rarita-Schwinger formalism, this approach generates explicit, covariant on-shell partial-wave amplitudes for two-body decays of massive particles of arbitrary spin, with definite orbital angular momentum and total final-state spin. This general framework provides a foundational Lorentz basis for hadronic reaction studies and $LS$-organized operators in theoretical investigations, such as Lattice QCD and QCD sum rules.
authors: Hao-Jie Jing, Shu-Ming Wu, Jia-Jun Wu

papers.title: Long-term yields of short-rate models as Feynman-Kac ground states: a variational quantum eigensolver with single-setting energy estimation on two NISQ platforms
papers.abstract: We show that the long-term yield of a short-rate model is the ground-state energy of a Schrodinger operator obtained from the Feynman-Kac bond-pricing equation, so that it can be computed by a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). We treat the Vasicek, Cox-Ingersoll-Ross and Black-Karasinski models; the last has no closed form. Calibrated monthly to the U.S. Treasury curve from 1985 to 2026, the long-term yield follows the 30-year yield with an in-sample correlation of 0.98. The Hamiltonian is stoquastic, so its ground state is positive and the energy can be estimated from computational-basis samples with a single measurement setting. On ibm_cleveland, gate noise appears mainly as bit flips of the high-order qubits.
